data.title: I Ported SAP to a 1976 CPU. It Wasn't That Slow
data.author: weinzierl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了zvdb-z80项目的基本信息。zvdb-z80是一个开源项目，用户可以对其进行复制（Fork）和标记星标（Star）。目前，该项目有1次复制和19个星标。文章还提到，要更改通知设置，用户必须登录。文章内容简短，主要涉及项目的基本互动和状态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对现代与旧式处理器优化、计算历史准确性、技术学习经历以及文章写作风格的讨论

不同观点：
• **关于现代与旧式处理器优化的讨论**：
   - _notreallyme_：认为在无MMU处理器和现代处理器上的代码优化截然不同。作者在频率高857倍的处理器上仅获得3到6倍的加速，表明旧的优化技巧在现代架构上显得非常慢。尽管执行流水线优化仍然有效，但不考虑缓存层次、内存管理方式和RAM访问时机将导致次优代码。
   - U1F984：质疑“查找表总是比计算快”的观点，认为由于现代内存速度远慢于CPU，现在的情形与过去不同。如果计算昂贵函数且查找表能放入L1缓存，查找表可能更快，但在主内存访问时间内可以进行大量计算。

• **关于计算历史准确性的讨论**：
   - Mr_Minderbinder：批评作者对计算历史的描述不准确。例如，1982/1983年的64K内存并不奢侈，C64作为廉价微型计算机即有此内存量。其他如昂贵的CPU周期和无浮点运算的说法也被认为是错误的。

• **关于技术学习经历的讨论**：
   - martinald：分享了在90年代末学习技术的经历，强调了由于经济限制，需要充分利用手头的设备进行学习和解决问题。

• **关于文章写作风格的讨论**：
   - orbifold：认为文章的写作风格和段落长度暗示其可能是AI生成。
   - bravesoul2：认为写作风格类似于LinkedIn上的销售文章。
   - faefox：认为文章明显的ChatGPT风格分散了对实际内容的注意力。
   - DrNosferatu：怀疑文章是否有LLM（语言模型）写作的成分。

补充讨论：
• **关于代码实现和项目细节的讨论**：
   - reidrac：指出Z80代码示例中的问题，如未使用的ix寄存器和不合理的循环计数器使用，认为代码有潜在错误。
   - mdaniel：提醒项目应添加许可证，以避免观众困惑。
   - IceDane：澄清“移植SAP”的说法，指出作者实际上是将自己为SAP平台编写的程序移植到1976年的处理器上，而非移植整个SAP系统。
   - renewiltord：认为文章具有点击诱饵性质，但同时也承认其有趣和具有娱乐性。

争议焦点：
• 作者对计算历史的描述是否准确。
• 在现代处理器上旧优化技巧的有效性。
• 文章是否由AI生成及其对内容的影响。
• 代码示例中的实现问题及其合理性。

data.title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
data.author: GavCo
data.article_summary: Biomni是一款通用的生物医学AI代理，旨在自动执行各种生物医学研究任务，通过整合大型语言模型（LLM）推理、检索增强规划和基于代码的执行，帮助科学家大幅提高研究效率并生成可测试的假设。用户可以通过设置脚本安装Biomni，并使用自然语言执行如CRISPR筛选、单细胞RNA测序注释和化合物ADMET性质预测等任务。Biomni是一个开放科学项目，鼓励社区贡献新工具、数据集、软件和基准等。当前正开发下一代版本Biomni-E2，贡献者将有机会在顶级期刊上共同署名发表论文。Biomni基于Apache-2.0许可证发布，但某些集成工具可能有更严格的商业许可证。更多信息和使用方法可访问biomni.stanford.edu。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个具有特定工具集和Python执行功能的智能代理系统在生物医学研究中的应用和潜力

不同观点：
• deepdarkforest：认为该系统通过预设的工具集和Python执行功能，能够有效缩小错误范围，尤其在处理标准化数据时具有优势。但也指出实际数据往往更复杂，工具的长期优势有待观察，特别是在处理专有数据集时。
• Edmond：看好该系统在科学研究中的潜力，并提到可能用于构建智能工作空间以辅助科研。
• andy99：关注该系统在生物威胁评估方面的风险，虽然对当前LLM的能力持怀疑态度，但认为该方向值得关注。
• joelthelion：质疑该系统在实际工作中的有效性和实用性，希望有业内人士提供意见。
• freedomben：对AI在医学研究和药物开发中的应用充满期待，认为AI在数据模式识别方面具有巨大潜力。
• teenvan_1995：对提供150多个工具的数量表示担忧，认为需要在实际应用中验证其有效性。
• dbcooper：询问是否有邀请名额，显示出对系统访问的兴趣。
• epistasis：对能够尝试该系统感到兴奋，表明其对该技术的前景看好。
• dmezzetti：分享了与生物医学文献分析相关的开源项目，提供了额外的技术资源和工具链接。
• AIorNot：将该系统推荐给在Crispr实验室工作的朋友，显示出对该系统实际应用的认可。
• SalmoShalazar：认为当前类似软件的泛滥表明创新有限，主要是围绕特定领域对LLM进行专业化包装，创新性不足。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：该系统在实际应用中的有效性和长期优势，特别是在处理复杂和专有数据集时的表现。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是该系统在生物威胁评估方面的潜在风险及其对科学研究的影响。
• 用户对工具数量和实际应用中的可行性表示关注，认为需要更多实际验证。
• 部分用户对AI在科学研究中的创新性和应用前景充满期待，并分享了相关资源和项目。

Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
Overview
Biomni is a general-purpose biomedical AI agent designed to autonomously execute a wide range of research tasks across diverse biomedical subfields. By integrating cutting-edge large language model (LLM) reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, Biomni helps scientists dramatically enhance research productivity and generate testable hypotheses.
Quick Start
Installation
Our software environment is massive and we provide a single setup.sh script to setup.
Follow this
file
to setup the env first.
Then activate the environment E1:
conda activate biomni_e1
then install the latest biomni package:
pip install biomni --upgrade
Or install from the github source version.
Lastly, configure your API keys in bash profile
~/.bashrc
:
export
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_API_KEY
"
export
OPENAI_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_API_KEY
"
#
optional if you just use Claude
Basic Usage
Once inside the environment, you can start using Biomni:
from
biomni
.
agent
import
A1
# Initialize the agent with data path, Data lake will be automatically downloaded on first run (~11GB)
agent
=
A1
(
path
=
'./data'
,
llm
=
'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'
)
# Execute biomedical tasks using natural language
agent
.
go
(
"Plan a CRISPR screen to identify genes that regulate T cell exhaustion, generate 32 genes that maximize the perturbation effect."
)
agent
.
go
(
"Perform scRNA-seq annotation at [PATH] and generate meaningful hypothesis"
)
agent
.
go
(
"Predict ADMET properties for this compound: CC(C)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)C(C)C(=O)O"
)
🤝 Contributing to Biomni
Biomni is an open-science initiative that thrives on community contributions. We welcome:
🔧 New Tools
: Specialized analysis functions and algorithms
📊 Datasets
: Curated biomedical data and knowledge bases
💻 Software
: Integration of existing biomedical software packages
📋 Benchmarks
: Evaluation datasets and performance metrics
📚 Misc
: Tutorials, examples, and use cases
🔧 Update existing tools
: many current tools are not optimized - fix and replacements are welcome!
Check out this
Contributing Guide
on how to contribute to the Biomni ecosystem.
If you have particular tool/database/software in mind that you want to add, you can also submit to
this form
and the biomni team will implement them.
🔬 Call for Contributors: Help Build Biomni-E2
Biomni-E1 only scratches the surface of what’s possible in the biomedical action space.
Now, we’re building
Biomni-E2
— a next-generation environment developed
with and for the community
.
We believe that by collaboratively defining and curating a shared library of standard biomedical actions, we can accelerate science for everyone.
Join us in shaping the future of biomedical AI agent.
Contributors with significant impact
(e.g., 10+ significant & integrated tool contributions or equivalent) will be
invited as co-authors
on our upcoming paper in a top-tier journal or conference.
All contributors
will be acknowledged in our publications.
More contributor perks...
Let’s build it together.

biomni.stanford.edu

data.title: The jank programming language
data.author: akkad33
data.article_summary: Jank是一种通用的编程语言，兼容Clojure，但通过C++和LLVM-based JIT实现，支持原生编译和最小运行时。它提供REPL开发环境，同时能够进行静态AOT编译生成原生可执行文件。Jank允许在Clojure代码中无缝嵌入C++代码，并支持多线程软件事务内存和反应代理系统。其编译器启动快、内存使用低，并提供高质量的错误报告。Jank还与Clojure生态工具（如Leiningen和nREPL）兼容，支持在同一文件中混合编写C++和Clojure代码。例子展示了如何利用Clojure强大的数据处理能力生成电影索引和转换字节大小为可读格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新语言Jank的开发、设计选择、名称、工具及其与Clojure的关系等的讨论。

不同观点：
• Jeaye（Jank的创建者）认为Jank通过LLVM和C++互操作性实现了独特的功能，如JIT编译和无缝的C++集成，且保留了Clojure的核心特性如nREPL。他计划在年底发布第一个alpha版本，并定期更新开发进展。
• Densh基于其在Scala Native上的经验，提出几点建议：避免提供向后兼容的JVM API子集，避免自己实现GC而是使用mmtk，重视多线程和并发，以及不过度优化单线程性能。
• Catfacts提到另一个类似的项目Clapp（Common Lisp在C++中使用LLVM），并指出Clapp的进展缓慢和编译时间长的问题。他对Jank能否避免类似问题表示关注，并建议从其他类似项目如ECL和Julia中吸取经验。
• Lisbbb对如何通过这些小众语言谋生表示疑问，回忆起Clojure在过去十几年的低迷，并对2025年还能看到Clojure或LISP的复兴表示惊讶。
• Mgdev表达了对项目的喜爱，但建议更改名称，以避免因名称问题在工作中受到限制。
• Norir建议采用一个更小的自举子集来简化设计，并通过C编译器和共享库实现REPL功能，认为当前的设计可能会导致不必要的复杂性。
• Lewdwig对Clojure曾经的辉煌和后来的停滞表示感慨，并希望Jank能为其带来新的活力。
• Jhoechtl提到与Janet语言的相关性。
• Padjo对Jank作为一个真实语言而不是一个深奥或玩笑语言表示惊讶。
• Lyngbakr关注Jank的工具链，希望其工具能像Gleam一样开箱即用。
• Defo10对Jank的错误报告功能表示期待，并希望看到与JVM的性能对比基准。

jank programming language - Clojure/LLVM/C++
The jank programming language
jank is a
general-purpose programming language
which embraces the
interactive, value-oriented
nature of Clojure as well as the desire for
native compilation and minimal runtimes
. jank is
strongly compatible with Clojure
and considers itself a dialect of Clojure. Please note that jank is under heavy development; assume all features are planned or incomplete.
Where jank differs from Clojure JVM is that its host is C++ on top of an
LLVM-based JIT
. This allows jank to offer the same benefits of
REPL-based development
while being able to
seamlessly reach into the native world
and compete seriously with JVM's performance.
Still, jank is a Clojure dialect and thus includes its
code-as-data philosophy and powerful macro system
. jank remains a functional-first language which builds upon Clojure's rich set of
persistent, immutable data structures
. When mutability is needed, jank offers a software transaction memory and reactive agent system to ensure
clean and correct multi-threaded designs
.
Current progress
Github
Sponsor
Wide spectrum dynamics
Enjoy both REPL iteration with JIT compilation and static AOT compilation to native executables.
01
Iterate like you would with Clojure
Iterate in the REPL and build your program from the ground up without leaving your editor.
(

& args
]
(

)]
(

game-state
)
(
end-game!
game-state
)
(
recur
(
next-state
game-state
)))))
02
Reach into the native world
Seamlessly switch to inline C++ within your Clojure source, while still having access to your Clojure code using interpolation.
(

create-vertex-shader!
[]
(
c++/glCreateShader
c++/GL_VERTEX_SHADER
))
(

[
shader source
]
(

[
shader

shader
)
source
(

source
)]
(
c++/glShaderSource
shader
1
source c++/nullptr
)))
(
defn
compile-shader!
[
shader
]
(
c++/glCompileShader
(
int
shader
)))
03
Compile to machine code
jank is built on an LLVM-based JIT. With AOT enabled, both statically and dynamically linked executables can be generated. The jank compiler itself has very speedy start times and low memory usage.
$
time
taskset
0x1
clj
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m1.127s
user
0m0.997s
sys
0m0.111s
$
time
taskset
0x1
jank
run
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m0.086s
user
0m0.045s
sys
0m0.040s
04
World-class errors
jank stands in its own category among lisps for its error reporting quality. No bloated JVM stack traces, opaque errors, or lack of context.
jank builds upon Clojure.
Keep your existing code; gain more confidence and more speed.
Strongly compatible with Clojure
If it works with Clojure JVM and it works with ClojureScript, it should work with jank. There's a
:jank
reader conditional for when you need it.
REPL and native JIT
Use your favorite nREPL editor plugin. jank uses an LLVM-based JIT to compile machine code on the fly.
Go native
Reach into native libraries or interact directly with your native code base. Seamlessly write both C++ and Clojure in the same file.
Tooling friendly
Leiningen, LSP, nREPL planned from the start. jank's compiler is also written with tooling in mind, so it can be used for lexing, parsing, and analysis.

44482273.article_summary: Jank是一种通用的编程语言，兼容Clojure，但通过C++和LLVM-based JIT实现，支持原生编译和最小运行时。它提供REPL开发环境，同时能够进行静态AOT编译生成原生可执行文件。Jank允许在Clojure代码中无缝嵌入C++代码，并支持多线程软件事务内存和反应代理系统。其编译器启动快、内存使用低，并提供高质量的错误报告。Jank还与Clojure生态工具（如Leiningen和nREPL）兼容，支持在同一文件中混合编写C++和Clojure代码。例子展示了如何利用Clojure强大的数据处理能力生成电影索引和转换字节大小为可读格式。

data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了发生在雷暴上方的神秘大气放电现象，包括红色精灵（red sprites）、绿色幽灵（green ghosts）和蓝色喷流（blue jets）。这些现象属于瞬态发光事件（TLEs），由雷暴产生的强大电场引发，通常发生在距地50至90公里的高空。红色精灵是最常见的TLEs，由正极闪电触发，呈现为短暂的红光，形状如同根系或水母。2022年，摄影师在青藏高原捕捉到105个红色精灵，并记录到罕见的喷流和幽灵现象。科学家正通过结合业余观测和专业研究，努力理解这些现象的成因及其与地球天气系统的关联。这些研究不仅满足了科学好奇心，还有助于更好地理解地面上的风暴系统。

44480363.article_content:
SCIENCE
The most otherworldly, mysterious forms of lightning on Earth
Scientists are working to understand the curious phenomena of red sprites, green ghosts and blue jets high above thunderstorms.
Red spites, a type of transient luminous event or TLE, appear in the upper atmosphere above a thunderstorm in Oklahoma in April 2025.
By
Isabel Swafford
Photographs by
Paul M Smith
June 26, 2025
Our atmosphere is like one big electrical circuit: Thunderstorms are the batteries that charge it up, and lightning is the current flowing through it. On the ground we see evidence of this circuit when lightning cracks and strikes the ground, or when it lights up deep inside a thundercloud, but high above the clouds lies a secret electrical zoo full of sprites, elves, and jets.
These fantastical terms refer to light displays called transient luminous events or TLEs that occur in Earth’s upper atmosphere during thunderstorms. “TLEs are mysterious, beautiful, and uniquely different from conventional lightning, yet they connect weather, space, and electricity in one dramatic moment. They occur high above the clouds, almost silently, and are invisible to most people—but they reflect powerful processes unfolding deep within thunderstorms,” says Hailiang Huang, a Ph.D. student at the University of Science and Technology of China who studies TLEs.
The very first photographic observations of these events in 1989 captured red flashes streaking across the sky in the blink of an eye. The displays were dubbed red sprites, inspired by characters in Shakespeare’s
A Midsummer Night’s Dream
, and a medley of other fairytale names followed, as researchers discovered new types of TLEs. Today, scientists are still working to understand these curious phenomena—what causes them, how often they happen, and what they can tell us about Earth’s atmosphere.
Red sprites, like these captured in December 2024 in Mississippi, are by far the most common TLE observed by both researchers and photographers.
A photographer snapped this image of red sprite lightning in June 2023 in Kansas. Some have described the flashes as looking like carrots or jellyfish.
What exactly are red sprites?
Just like storm chasing, some photographers have taken to sprite chasing, searching for elusive red sprites and other TLEs above nighttime thunderstorms.
(
See rare colorful lightning sprites dance above a hurricane
.)
Red sprites have been observed off the coast of Europe and over the U.S. Great Plains, but in 2022, astrophotographers Angel An and Shuchang Dong captured 105 red sprites, the largest number ever seen in a single thunderstorm in South Asia,
researchers recently
reported in the journal
Advances in Atmospheric Science
.
4th of July Sale - 25% OFF!
Magazine for all ages starting at $25/year
SEE SUBSCRIPTION OPTIONS
“Red sprites are the most iconic [of TLEs],” says Huang, the lead author of the paper.
They flash into existence for just a fraction of a second in a spindly root-like system of red streaks. The phenomenon is caused by positive lightning that strikes the ground, creating an electric field that reaches up into the atmosphere, about 50 to 90 kilometers above Earth.
On the Tibetan Plateau, north of the Himalayas, thunderstorms are very common. The dramatic changes in elevation produce intense convection in the atmosphere and the churning of wet air creates clouds—a rich laboratory for studying TLEs. Yet none had been recorded there until An and Dong’s storm imagery in 2022.
Huang and his collaborator
Gaopeng Lu
, an atmospheric physicist at the University of Science and Technology of China, developed a method to synchronize the videos and photos that An and Dong took on the Tibetan Plateau. Using satellite data and maps of the stars in the night sky to determine the timestamps of each video frame, the team linked around 70 percent of verified sprites to the parent lightning that triggered them.
To Huang, the results demonstrate the scientific value of amateur observations. “It’s exciting that this field brings together professional scientists and passionate amateurs, working side by side to understand something so ephemeral, yet so profound.”
Not only did the photographers capture a significant number of red sprites, the Himalayan storm also featured even rarer TLEs called jets and ghosts. The team found 16 secondary jets, powerful columns of often blue or purple light darting upwards into the sky, and at least four
ghosts
, green hazy glows that can sometimes hover above red sprites.
“While sprites [and other TLEs] may appear delicate and silent in the upper atmosphere, they are often linked to powerful, sometimes devastating weather systems,” says Huang. “Understanding them not only satisfies our curiosity about the upper atmosphere, but also helps us learn more about the storms we face here on Earth.”

data.author: samwcurry
data.article_summary: 本文描述了研究人员在麦当劳招聘聊天机器人平台McHire中发现的安全漏洞。该平台由Paradox.ai开发，使用Olivia机器人收集求职者的个人信息和偏好。研究人员通过简单默认凭证（123456:123456）登录系统，并发现一个不安全的直接对象引用（IDOR）漏洞，可访问超过6400万求职者的个人数据，包括姓名、联系方式、申请状态和聊天记录。研究人员立即向Paradox.ai和麦当劳披露了该漏洞，随后漏洞被迅速修复。Paradox.ai也表示保护候选人和客户数据是其首要任务，并承诺进行进一步审查以防止类似问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Paradox.ai及相关安全漏洞、人格测试和招聘过程的讨论

不同观点：
• **ryandrake**：对人格测试的有效性提出质疑，认为测试题目容易猜测，像是让申请者知道何时该“撒谎”以迎合雇主。
• **david2ndaccount**：关注安全问题的披露过程，指出由于缺乏公开的披露联系方式，不得不通过随机发送邮件来解决问题，并对Paradox.ai的安全页面表示不满。
• **Daviey**：对问题是否属于不安全直接对象引用（IDOR）提出不同看法，认为问题核心在于认证机制的薄弱，而非IDOR。引用了OWASP的定义，并指出问题更符合CWE-1390和CWE-306。
• **Proofread0592**：对使用简单密码如“123456”感到惊讶，将其比作笑话。
• **bravesoul2**：指出AI并非问题原因，问题在于对象ID的枚举，并提到通过简单密码进入测试站点进行尝试。
• **Gelob**：提到Fedex也使用Paradox.ai，并对其表现表示不满。
• **macqm**：指出Paradox.ai多年来未修复漏洞，曾能通过Google索引找到包含个人敏感信息的对话，尽管现在增加了验证步骤，但仍泄露全邮箱和电话号码。
• **Titan2189**：赞赏Paradox在报告后30小时内修复了漏洞。
• **snypher**：对使用简单密码“123456”进入系统表示好奇，希望了解更多背后的故事。
• **ge96**：回忆曾需回答行为问题以申请McD's职位，问题涉及伦理抉择。
• **bombcar**：对McDonald's在安全漏洞响应方面的表现表示赞赏，认为其表现优于许多互联网公司。
• **combinator_y**：指出企业内部缺乏控制，提到具体例子（“NGA FS”）。
• **trod1234**：对McDonald's声称有6400万申请者表示怀疑，认为数字不合理，质疑公司是否通过虚假招聘广告误导求职者。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：问题的定性，Daviey认为不应简单归类为IDOR，而应关注认证机制的缺陷。
• **安全漏洞的具体表现**：包括简单密码、敏感信息泄露、缺乏多因素认证（MFA）等。
• **对公司招聘和安全实践的质疑**：如招聘广告的真实性和企业内部控制问题。
• **对Paradox.ai的评价**：既有对其安全漏洞修复速度的赞赏，也有对其长期存在漏洞的不满。

44513940.article_content:
Would you like an IDOR with that? Leaking 64 million McDonald’s job applications
Introduction
McHire
is the chatbot recruitment platform used by
90%
of McDonald’s franchisees. Prospective employees chat with a bot named Olivia, created by a company called
Paradox.ai
, that collects their personal information, shift preferences, and administers personality tests. We noticed this after seeing complaints on Reddit of the bot
responding with nonsensical answers
.
During a cursory security review of a few hours, we identified two serious issues: the McHire administration interface for restaurant owners accepted the default credentials
123456:123456
, and an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) on an internal API allowed us to access any contacts and chats we wanted. Together they allowed us and anyone else with a McHire account and access to any inbox to retrieve the personal data of more than 64 million applicants.
Applying for a job
We started by applying for a job at our local McDonald’s. McHire has a consumer-facing site at
https://jobs.mchire.com/
where it is easy to find available postings near you. We were immediately sent to Olivia, who helped us fill in our email and phone number along with what shifts we can work, and we were instantly moved to the next stage: the personality test!
McHire personality test
The personality test was a disturbing experience powered by
Traitify.com
where we were asked if phrases like “enjoys overtime” are either
Me
or
Not Me
. It was simple to guess that we should probably select
Me
for the pro-employer questions and
Not Me
for questions referencing being argumentative or aggressive, but it was still quite strange.
Unfortunately, after this, we were stuck without any further progress and appeared to be awaiting human review. We tried to prompt inject the Olivia chatbot, which likely ruined our chance at a human approving us, but it seemed to be locked to a list of pre-set responses or something similar, and there were no interesting APIs for the candidates.
Logging in
We noticed that restaurant owners can login to view applicants at
https://www.mchire.com/signin
. Although the app tries to force SSO for McDonald’s, there is a smaller link for “Paradox team members” that caught our eye.
Without much thought, we entered “123456” as the username and “123456” as the password and were surprised to see we were immediately logged in!
McHire user administration
It turned out we had become the administrator of a test restaurant inside the McHire system. We could see all of the employees of the restaurant were simply employees of Paradox.ai, the company behind McHire. This was great because we could now see how the app worked, but annoying because we had still not demonstrated any actual confidentiality or integrity impact.
Applying for our job
We decided to apply to one of the test job postings the account had set up already and see what it looked like on the other side. The restaurant can view all of the in-progress conversations with “Olivia” and then intervene when they hit certain stages like having completed the personality test.
Restaurant’s view of our conversation application
While viewing our test conversations, we noticed an interesting API to fetch the candidate information
PUT /api/lead/cem-xhr
, which seems to be a reference to proxying to some kind of Customer or Candidate Experience Manager (CEM) via an XHR request. The main parameter of this request was the
lead_id
of the chat, which for our test applicant was about
64,185,742
. We tried decrementing this number, and were immediately faced with PII from another McDonald’s applicant (including “unmasked” contact data)!
We quickly realized this API allows us to access every chat interaction that has ever applied for a job at McDonald’s. The information returned included:
Name, email address, phone number, address
Candidacy state and every state change/form input the candidate had submitted (shifts they could work, etc)
Auth token to log into the consumer UI as that user, leaking their raw chat messages and presumably other information
We immediately began disclosure of this issue once we realized the potential impact. Unfortunately, no disclosure contacts were publicly available and we had to resort to emailing random people. The
Paradox.ai security page
just says that we do not have to worry about security!
After our outreach reached the appropriate people, the
Paradox.ai
team engaged with us, emphasized that safeguarding candidate and client data was their top priority, promptly remediated the vulnerability, and committed to further reviews to identify and close any remaining avenues of exploitation.
Disclosure
We disclosed this issue to
Paradox.ai
and McDonald’s at the same time.
06/30/2025 5:46PM ET:
Disclosed to
Paradox.ai
and McDonald’s
06/30/2025 6:24PM ET:
McDonald’s confirms receipt and requests technical details
06/30/2025 7:31PM ET:
Credentials are no longer usable to access the app
07/01/2025 9:44PM ET:

data.title: The Origin of the Research University
data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了研究型大学的起源，特别是19世纪德国大学如何从以教学为主的中世纪机构转变为兼具教学与研究的现代大学模式。在此之前，大学并非新知识生产的主要场所，学术研究多在如英国皇家学会等机构进行。然而，19世纪的德国大学通过将研究纳入其体系，迅速成为知识生产的核心，推动了化学、物理学、细胞理论、细菌学和科学医学等领域的重大进展。这一变革不仅使德国大学主导了当时的学术界，还影响了整个欧洲乃至后来的美国大学体系。文章还讨论了为何这一变革发生在政治分裂、科学氛围薄弱的德国，以及这一历史对当今学术界面临的挑战有何启示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术体系的历史、现状及其问题

不同观点：
• [bonoboTP] 认为19世纪前的许多重要知识分子并非在大学体系内工作，而现代学术界倾向于将自己塑造成知识的唯一传承者和开拓者。此外， peer review、影响因子等机制缺乏历史背景和替代方案的讨论，学生在学术体系中缺乏反思和元认知的机会。
• [megaloblasto] 对美国研究型大学感到失望，认为这些大学更关注研究影响而非本科教育质量。大学利用学生作为稳定收入来源，而教育质量却得不到保障，学生的利益受损。
• [djoldman] 通过分享圣学术节骚乱的历史事件，暗示过去的学生行为问题，反映出不同时期的大学文化和学生纪律问题。
• [ricksunny] 提到一位前MIT林肯实验室研究员的工作，强调19世纪中期至战前德国技术专家对科学和历史的贡献，提供了一个具体的历史参考。
• [dr_dshiv] 认为亚历山大港的Mouseion是研究型大学的起源，强调其在人文和科学方面的贡献，并持续了几百年，提供了一个古代学术机构的例子。
• [dlcarrier] 认为教育和学术应该分离，暗示当前的体系存在问题。
• [mistrial9] 对某些对学术历史的不严谨描述提出批评，认为一些概括性的陈述缺乏可信度，同时对学术资历和无意义出版物的问题提出见解。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个历史例子和资源链接，如圣学术节骚乱和德国技术专家的贡献，提供了具体的历史背景和参考资料。
• 争议的焦点包括学术体系的历史描述的可信度和现代学术机制（如peer review和影响因子）的讨论不足。
• 反思和元认知在学术教育中的重要性也被提出，强调学生对学术体系本身的理解和批判性思考能力。

总结：评论中主要讨论了学术体系的历史演变、现代大学教育的问题以及学术机制的反思。不同评论者从历史背景、个人经历和学术机制等角度提出了各自的观点和批评。争议点主要集中在历史描述的准确性和现代学术机制的合理性上。

44484409.article_content:
The Origin of the Research University
Clara Collier
Universities have existed for more than a thousand years — and for almost all of that time, they weren’t centers of research. What changed in 19th century Germany?
If you were alive in 1800 and someone asked you about the future of research, it wouldn’t occur to you to mention the university. Real scholarship happened in new, modern, enlightened institutions like the British Royal Society or the French
Académie des sciences.
Universities were a medieval relic. And nowhere was it more medieval, hidebound, and generally dysfunctional than in the German-speaking world.
But something happened to German universities at the turn of the 19th century — they developed a new system that combined teaching with research. Within a few decades, everyone in Europe was trying to copy their model. German scientists dominated chemistry and revolutionized modern physics. They came up with cell theory, bacteriology, the whole laboratory-based model of scientific medicine, and I don’t think it’s much of a stretch to say that they invented the social sciences in almost full generality. By the end of the century, they were the greatest engine of organized knowledge production the world had ever seen — and if they’ve since been surpassed by the American university system, that’s mostly because we copied them.
I think we don't properly appreciate how surprising this is. It’s odd that the research university exists at all. Universities have been around for a thousand years, but for most of their history, they were not seen as institutions for producing new knowledge. It’s even stranger that it came to be in a land which was politically fragmented, lacked a strong scientific community, and had very limited interest in creating one.
So I can’t help but ask: Why Germany? Why universities? Why does the entire modern institutional research ecosystem look the way it does? Does this history have anything to tell us about how to navigate an era of intense hostility and pessimism towards academia? (No promises!) Who made this thing? Were they even trying to? And why does it work so well?
Bibliotheca Büloviana Acaddemae, Georgiae Augustae donata Göttinga, engraved by Georg Daniel Heumann (1691–1759). Göttingen University Library, founded in 1734, was considered the first academic research library.
German universities in the age of Enlightenment
Scholars at early modern universities did research — but it was on their own time. Universities in early modern Europe were teaching institutions. Their primary purpose was to produce priests, lawyers, and doctors. To this end, they had four traditional faculties: theology, law, medicine, and what the Germans called philosophy.  This last included everything
that might be part of a modern arts and sciences education — any subject, from poetry to physics, which wasn’t directly pre-professional. Of the four, it  was by far the least prestigious and worst attended. Professors were paid exclusively for lecturing, usually not very much, and professors of the arts and sciences were paid the least of all.
Starting in the 16th century, these factors tended to push the people most interested in advancing human knowledge outside of universities. The trend started in astronomy. Copernicus, Brahe, and Galileo all began their careers as university professors, and all left for positions as civil servants or court astronomers which offered more money and more freedom. (Kepler, because of his heterodox approach to Lutheranism, was never able to secure a university chair at all.) Some universities tried to invest in experimental facilities — an observatory at Utrecht, a chemical laboratory at Altdorf — but these couldn’t compete with the great private or government-funded facilities being built in England and France. While many intellectuals stayed in academia, leading scholars were more and more likely to take up better offers elsewhere. The intellectual center of gravity shifted from universities to the international republic of letters.
German universities in the Age of Enlightenment shared all of these problems and more. Their curriculum was, quite literally, medieval. So were their endowments. Hiring was rife with nepotism — and even when it didn’t involve replacing a professor with someone’s son or son-in-law, it was loosely related to any modern conception of academic merit. Specialization was non-existent. It hardly mattered if a professor of oriental languages could read Hebrew or Arabic, so long as he had adequate seniority, and a poetry professor who wanted a raise might well be handed an additional chair in mathematics. The students were menaces, given to drunkenness, gambling, dueling, and chronically skipping class.
Everyone agreed that German universities needed to change. But very few people thought that this should involve making them centers of free intellectual inquiry. Instead, Enlightenment critics wanted them to be
useful
. A scholar of the 17th

data.title: Show HN: I built a playground to showcase what Flux Kontext is good at
data.author: Zephyrion
data.article_summary: Flux Kontext Dev是一款免费的在线AI图像编辑工具，无需注册，可即时使用。用户上传图片并描述所需修改，工具将自动完成编辑。它支持修改图像元素、照片修复与上色、照片风格转换、文字编辑、Logo增强、去除人群以及产品展示等多种功能。该工具基于FLUX.1 Kontext [dev]模型，拥有120亿参数，针对消费级硬件优化，并兼容多种推理框架。它提供开放权重，供研究和非商业使用，具有高性能和精确的编辑能力，是开源图像编辑技术的新标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kontext模型的功能、可用性、技术问题及其实际效果的争议

不同观点：
• **vunderba的观点**：Kontext模型在图像编辑方面有革命性意义，能够对图像局部进行修改而不影响其他部分，节省了遮罩和修复的时间。他还提到该模型支持多图像合成，展示了其强大功能。
• **roenxi的观点**：虽然Kontext模型的发布被延迟，且未公开权重导致无法商用，但其在公众领域的出现仍是一个进步，超越了稳定扩散模型的简单提示词机制。
• **bsenftner的观点**：质疑提供公共访问的财务支持，怀疑背后是否有大型组织或资金支持，而非个人行为。
• **chrismorgan的观点**：对“AI精度”持怀疑态度，指出Kontext在图像修复和着色方面仍存在一些问题，如图像重构和现实性，并建议更严谨的修改前后对比。
• **merelysounds和fazza999、shekhar101的观点**：在使用Kontext时遇到错误信息，处理失败，对用户体验表示失望，并与其他工具（如MidJourney）进行对比。
• **winterrx和mg的观点**：关注Kontext模型的运行成本及服务器问题，好奇其免费服务的财务可持续性和技术实现方式。

补充讨论：
• **商业可用性**：roenxi指出Kontext模型未公开权重，限制了商业应用。
• **技术问题**：多个用户（merelysounds、fazza999、shekhar101）报告使用过程中遇到错误，影响使用体验。
• **功能展示与对比**：chrismorgan建议更严谨的对比方式以展示模型的修改效果。
• **财务与技术支持**：bsenftner、winterrx和mg关注模型提供免费访问的财务支持和运行方式。

data.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Memory Safety Sanitizers
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇关于C/C++内存安全检测工具评估的论文及其相关技术的讨论

不同观点：
• pizlonator认为，该论文没有提到作者之前的工作MESH，也没有将其纳入评估，这令人费解。他还对论文中的测试案例是否公开以及它们能否有效检测问题表示好奇。
• rwmj质疑论文中关于“通过牺牲内存安全性来提升性能”的说法，并提出先进的编译器和CPU可能已经能解决部分边界检查问题。他还提到高级编程语言可以通过使用map、fold等函数来避免此类问题，但此处讨论的是C语言。
• osivertsson提供了论文的下载链接，绕过了付费墙的限制。
• Ygg2引用了论文的结论，指出目前没有任何一种清理工具能够完全实现时间和空间上的内存安全，并详细说明了各类工具在检测内存错误方面的不足。
• ape4建议论文标题应更明确地指出其关注的是C/C++，或者认为这是众所周知的。
• bgwalter质疑为何在SoftBound+CETS表现最佳的情况下，Fraunhofer不资助创建一个Debian包，并指出其未维护的状态。
• lou1306对Infer工具未被纳入评估表示惊讶，指出其支持C/C++，并且其基于分离逻辑的推理框架非常适合用于检查内存安全。
• unpaydijk提到论文在付费墙后，无法访问。

补充讨论：
• 关于MESH未被纳入评估的争议是讨论中的一个焦点，pizlonator对此表示困惑。
• 对各类工具检测效果的评价是另一个重要讨论点，尤其是Ygg2引用的结论，指出了现有工具的不足。
• 对SoftBound+CETS的讨论涉及其为何未被广泛应用和维护的问题，bgwalter对此表示不解。
• 对Infer工具的遗漏也引起了lou1306的注意，并提出了其在检测内存安全方面的潜在价值。

总的来说，讨论围绕论文的内容、方法及其未涵盖的其他相关技术展开，涉及工具的选择、评估的全面性以及各类技术在实际应用中的表现和局限。

data.title: Matt Trout has died
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这则回复表达了作者对与Matt相处时光的怀念。作者提到他们曾有过许多美好的时刻，尽管也有些不如意的时光。在Matt离开或发生变故的时刻，美好的回忆让作者微笑，但也让作者感到悲伤，因为不再有机会创造更多美好的回忆。整体表达了一种对过去美好时光的留恋和对未来无法继续的遗憾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Perl社区重要人物Matt Trout（mst）去世的悼念及其影响和评价

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
   - Matt是Perl社区的重要贡献者，开发了如Catalyst、DBIx::Class和Moo等重要软件包，这些工具在Perl开发中极具影响力，且少有其他语言的工具能与之媲美（ShamblingMound）。
   - 他对社区的贡献不仅限于技术，还帮助许多人成长，推动他们参与社区活动，甚至改变了一些人的职业生涯（ether_at_cpan, xantronix）。
   - 尽管他有时因固执己见而与他人产生冲突，但他在处理这些冲突时表现出色，并致力于建立Perl社区的行为准则（xantronix, petesergeant）。

• 复杂评价：
   - Matt的性格具有挑战性，有些人认为他难以相处，甚至抢走朋友的女友，但他在职业和生活上的建议对一些人产生了积极影响（Slortibort, kodzoman）。
   - 他是一个天才，但有时因过于坚持自己的想法而得罪人（ShamblingMound, petesergeant）。

• 个人缅怀：
   - 许多人表达了个人悲痛和怀念之情，分享了与Matt共事的经历和对他的感激（xantronix, _rpf, rurban, martinclayton）。
   - 他的去世对Perl社区是一个重大损失，他的工作和贡献将继续影响许多人（IncandescentGas, mst的HN链接）。

补充讨论：
• Matt的去世消息在多个平台引发悼念，他的工作和人格对Perl社区产生了深远影响（jasonjayr, layer8, xena）。
• 一些人提到他在Perl社区的争议性，但总体上对他的贡献和影响持肯定态度（petesergeant）。
• 具体的技术贡献如DBIx::Class和Catalyst仍被广泛使用，并在Perl开发中占据重要地位（ShamblingMound, martinclayton）。

争议焦点：
• Matt的性格和行为方式在社区中具有两面性，有些人认为他难以相处，但大多数人认可他的专业能力和对社区的贡献（Slortibort, ShamblingMound, petesergeant）。

44518269.article_content:
This makes me sad.  I had many good times with Matt, and some less than awesome times, but at moments like this, the good times bring a smile to my face.  It makes me sad I will no longer be able to look forwardto any more good times.

data.title: Show HN: BreakerMachines – Modern Circuit Breaker for Rails with Async Support
data.author: seuros
data.article_summary: BreakerMachines 是一个为 Ruby 和 Rails 设计的现代电路断路器库，具有线程安全、支持异步和纤维（fiber）、内置回退机制、高效内存使用和监控等特点。它基于 state_machines 构建，支持对分布式系统的保护，防止级联故障。该库提供对冲请求、多后端支持、百分比阈值、动态断路器和丰富的回调与检测功能。此外，它还集成了 ActiveSupport::Notifications，并提供详细的文档和多种测试指南。BreakerMachines 旨在解决微服务架构中的常见问题，如过度重试导致的自我 DDoS 攻击，帮助开发者构建更健壮的系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同技术（如令牌桶与断路器）在处理系统故障和扩展性问题时的优劣比较，以及对一个具体实现（BreakerMachines）的反馈和建议。

不同观点：
• [grogenaut] 认为令牌桶（Token Bucket）比断路器（Circuit Breakers）更优。理由是断路器本质上是双模态的，会在不发送请求和突发大量请求之间切换，这可能在高规模系统中引发内存、垃圾回收、负载均衡和自动扩展问题。令牌桶则能更平滑地调节系统压力，类似于老式恒温器和PID控制回路的区别。

Async Ruby is the Future of AI Apps (And It's Already Here)
Carmine Paolino
Jul 9, 2025
After a decade as an ML engineer/scientist immersed in Python’s async ecosystem, returning to Ruby felt like stepping back in time. Where was the async revolution? Why was everyone still using threads for everything? SolidQueue, Sidekiq, GoodJob – all thread-based. Even newer solutions defaulted to the same concurrency model.
Coming from Python, where the entire community had reorganized around
asyncio
, this seemed bizarre. FastAPI replaced Flask. Every library spawned an async twin. The transformation was total and necessary.
Then, building
RubyLLM
and
Chat with Work
, I noticed that
LLM communication is async Ruby’s killer app
. The unique demands of streaming AI responses – long-lived connections, token-by-token delivery, thousands of concurrent conversations – expose exactly why async matters.
Here’s the exciting bit: once I understood Ruby’s approach to async, I realized it’s actually
superior
to Python’s. While Python forced everyone to rewrite their entire stack, Ruby quietly built something better. Your existing code just works. No syntax changes. No library migrations. Just better performance when you need it.
The async ecosystem that
Samuel Williams
and others have been building for years suddenly makes perfect sense. We just needed the right use case to see it.
Why LLM Communication Breaks Everything
LLM applications create a perfect storm of challenges that expose every weakness in thread-based concurrency:
1. Slot Starvation
Configure any thread-based job queue with 25 workers:
class
StreamAIResponseJob
<
ApplicationJob
def
perform
(
chat
,
message
)
# This job occupies 1 of your 25 slots...
chat
.
ask
(
message
)
do
|
chunk
|
# ...for the ENTIRE streaming duration (30-60 seconds)
broadcast_chunk
(
chunk
)
# Thread is 99% idle, just waiting for tokens
end
# Slot only freed here, after full response
end
end
Your 26th user? They’re waiting in line. Not because your server is busy, but because all your workers are occupied by jobs waiting for tokens.
2. Resource Multiplication
Each thread needs its own:
Database connection (25 threads = 25 connections minimum)
Stack memory allocation
OS thread management overhead
For 1000 concurrent conversations, you’d need 1000 threads. Each thread needs its database connection. That’s 1000 database connections for threads that are 99% idle.
3. Performance Overhead
Real benchmarks show
1
:
Creating a thread: ~80μs
Thread context switch: ~1.3μs
Maximum throughput: ~5,000 requests/second
When you’re handling thousands of streaming connections, these microseconds add up to real latency.
4. Scalability Challenges
Try creating 10,000 threads and the OS scheduler starts to struggle. The overhead becomes crushing. Yet modern AI apps need to handle thousands of concurrent conversations.
These aren’t separate issues – they’re all symptoms of the same architectural mismatch. LLM communication is fundamentally different from traditional background jobs.
Understanding Concurrency: Threads vs Async
To understand why LLM applications are async’s perfect use case – and why Ruby’s implementation is so elegant – we need to build up from first principles.
The Hierarchy: Processes, Threads, and Fibers
Think of your computer as an office building:
Processes
are like separate offices – each with its own locked door, furniture, and files. They can’t see into each other’s spaces (memory isolation).
Threads
are like workers sharing the same office – they can access the same filing cabinets (shared memory) but need to coordinate to avoid collisions.
Fibers
are like multiple tasks juggled by one worker at their desk – switching between them manually when waiting for something (like a phone call).
Scheduling: The Core Difference
The fundamental question in concurrency is: who decides when to switch between tasks?
Threads: Preemptive Multitasking
With threads, the operating system is the boss. It forcibly interrupts running threads to give others a turn:
# You start threads, but the OS controls them
threads
=
10
.
times
.
map
do
|
i
|
Thread
.
new
do
# This might be interrupted at ANY point
expensive_calculation
(
i
)
fetch_from_api
(
i
)
# Each thread blocks individually here
process_result
(
i
)
end
end
Each thread:
Gets scheduled by the OS kernel
Can be interrupted mid-execution (in Ruby, after 100ms)
Blocks individually on I/O operations
Requires OS resources and kernel data structures
Needs its own resources (like database connections)
Fibers: Cooperative Concurrency
With fibers, switching is voluntary – they only yield at I/O boundaries:
# Fibers yield control cooperatively
Async
do
fibers
=
10
.
times
.
map
do
|
i
|
Async
do
expensive_calculation
(
i
)
# Runs to completion
fetch_from_api
(
i
)
# Yields here, other fibers run

(
i
)
# Continues after I/O completes
end
end

Schedules itself by yielding during I/O

data.title: How to prove false statements: Practical attacks on Fiat-Shamir
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 计算机科学家发现了一种方法可以证明谎言，揭示了区块链和其他数字加密方案中的一个显著安全问题。传统上，计算机程序依赖哈希函数来生成看似随机的数据，并假设这些输出与真正的随机性无异，这一假设被称为随机预言模型。然而，一篇新论文颠覆了这一基础假设，展示了一种欺骗商用证明系统来验证虚假陈述的方法。该系统在随机预言模型下是安全的，但研究人员发现，无论使用何种哈希函数生成“随机性”，他们都能够证明谎言。这一发现对区块链和加密货币交易等依赖此类证明协议的系统构成了威胁，因为这些系统需要通过外部服务器验证计算。该研究引发了对随机预言模型的重新思考，并凸显了修复这些漏洞的紧迫性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章及相关协议攻击的技术细节和理解的讨论

不同观点：
• GTP认为文章缺乏细节，并指出攻击是基于协议前提的破坏，与随机预言模型关系不大。他质疑如果被诱骗接受恶意程序，协议会失效，并提到验证程序有效性应在协议外进行。他还质疑是否应在随机预言模型下难以写入包含自身哈希的程序。
• PretzelPirate指出文章缺乏时间线，并提到以太坊研究人员自2020年以来就在讨论相关内容，质疑他们对该工作不熟悉的描述。
• tempodox关注该漏洞对加密货币（如比特币）交易的影响，寻求更通俗易懂的解释。
• baby提供了一个白板会议链接，讨论相关内容。

An attack on a fundamental proof technique reveals a glaring security issue for blockchains and other digital encryption schemes.

Randomness is a source of power. From the coin toss that decides which team gets the ball to the random keys that secure online interactions, randomness lets us make choices that are fair and impossible to predict.
But in many computing applications, suitable randomness can be hard to generate. So instead, programmers often rely on things called hash functions, which swirl data around and extract some small portion in a way that looks random. For decades, many computer scientists have presumed that for practical purposes, the outputs of good hash functions are generally indistinguishable from genuine randomness — an assumption they call the random oracle model.
“It’s hard to find today a cryptographic application… whose security analysis does not use this methodology,” said
Ran Canetti
of Boston University.
Now, a
new paper
has shaken that bedrock assumption. It demonstrates a method for tricking a commercially available proof system into certifying false statements, even though the system is demonstrably secure if you accept the random oracle model. Proof systems related to this one are essential for the blockchains that record cryptocurrency transactions, where they are used to certify computations performed by outside servers.
There’s “a lot of money relying on this stuff,” said
Eylon Yogev
of Bar-Ilan University in Israel. For blockchain proof protocols, “there’s a huge motivation for attackers to break the security of the system.”
In the new paper — by
Dmitry Khovratovich
of the Ethereum Foundation,
Ron Rothblum
of the zero-knowledge proof technology company Succinct and the Technion in Haifa, Israel, and Lev Soukhanov of the blockchain-focused start-up [[alloc] init] — the researchers are able to prove lies no matter which hash function is used to generate the “randomness” the proof system relies upon.
When Yogev heard about the team’s result, he said, “I had the feeling that someone is pulling the carpet from under my feet.” He and others have been working to patch up these vulnerabilities. But “it’s far from being a solved issue,” he said.
More broadly, the new result is forcing a reckoning about the random oracle model. “This is a time to rethink,” Canetti said.
A Mathematical Blender
A host of different computing applications — from cryptocurrencies to cloud computing — involve convincing a bunch of strangers on the internet that you’ve performed a computation correctly. The new paper shows how to hijack a fundamental technique that enables people to certify such computations. The technique, called the Fiat-Shamir transformation, is useful not just in blockchains and cloud computing but also in many other cryptographic applications, such as the key exchanges that safeguard web transactions and encrypt text messages. It’s so ubiquitous that it has become a verb, as in “Let’s Fiat-Shamir this.”
Ron Rothblum, together with Dmitry Khovratovich and Lev Soukhanov, have upended the prevailing thinking on a fundamental proof technique.
Courtesy of Ron Rothblum
The Fiat-Shamir transformation is used in settings where you can verify a computation by inspecting it in random spots. For instance, if a professor has assigned 100 problems for homework but doesn’t want to grade a student’s entire assignment, she can randomly choose 10 problems to grade. In the language of computer scientists, she is making 10 “random challenges” to the student’s homework. If the answers to those 10 problems are correct, the professor can feel confident that most of the other answers are correct too. (There are ways to modify this setup if she wants to be convinced that the student got every single problem right, not just most of them.)
This particular scenario would probably play out on the professor’s desk. But since the Fiat-Shamir transformation is about convincing a bunch of distant strangers, let’s instead imagine that the student wants to prove the correctness of his homework not just to the professor, but to an entire auditorium full of people.
Imagine that the student starts by “turning in” his assignment by locking each of his answers in a separate box. 44519175.article_summary: 计算机科学家发现了一种方法可以证明谎言，揭示了区块链和其他数字加密方案中的一个显著安全问题。传统上，计算机程序依赖哈希函数来生成看似随机的数据，并假设这些输出与真正的随机性无异，这一假设被称为随机预言模型。然而，一篇新论文颠覆了这一基础假设，展示了一种欺骗商用证明系统来验证虚假陈述的方法。该系统在随机预言模型下是安全的，但研究人员发现，无论使用何种哈希函数生成“随机性”，他们都能够证明谎言。这一发现对区块链和加密货币交易等依赖此类证明协议的系统构成了威胁，因为这些系统需要通过外部服务器验证计算。该研究引发了对随机预言模型的重新思考，并凸显了修复这些漏洞的紧迫性。

data.title: Radiocarbon dating reveals Rapa Nui not as isolated as previously thought
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 考古学研究通过放射性碳定年法揭示，复活节岛（Rapa Nui）并非之前认为的那样孤立。研究表明，波利尼西亚的仪式活动和纪念性建筑存在东西方双向传播。最初，人类从西波利尼西亚（如汤加和萨摩亚）向东迁徙，建立了包括复活节岛在内的定居点。然而，研究发现，东波利尼西亚的仪式场所（如马拉埃石台）在时间上早于西方，表明东方的仪式理念后来反馈影响了西方。这挑战了复活节岛孤立发展的传统观点，显示岛屿间存在复杂的互动网络。研究强调，尽管最初的迁徙是从西到东，但随后的文化发展更为复杂，存在东向西的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复活节岛的波利尼西亚居民到达时间及其对环境的影响

不同观点：
• 传统观点认为，波利尼西亚居民在公元800年左右到达复活节岛，这一结论基于早期研究证据。
• 2007年的一项研究（由考古学家Terry Hunt等进行）提供了新证据，表明居民到达时间更接近公元1200年。这一发现推迟了人类对岛上环境影响的时间线。
• Hunt的团队通过在Anakena海滩的考古挖掘，结合放射性碳定年法，得出了公元1200年到达的结论，这比传统观点晚了四个世纪。

补充讨论：
• Hunt认为，人类对环境的破坏速度可能被高估了，单靠人类无法如此迅速地摧毁森林。他提出，波利尼西亚鼠的大量繁殖对森林的破坏起到了关键作用。
  - 证据包括在挖掘中发现的大量鼠骨，以及鼠对棕榈树种子的啃食。
  - Hunt推测，鼠群在短短几年内可以达到数百万，吃掉所有种子，阻止森林再生，从而加速森林退化。
  - 人类砍伐和燃烧树木的活动进一步加剧了这一过程，最终导致环境崩溃。
  
• 争议焦点在于岛上人口的迅速增长和环境的急剧恶化时间线。传统观点与Hunt的新发现之间的矛盾，引发了对岛上生态和社会系统崩溃原因的重新审视。

• 支持Hunt理论的论据包括：在考古挖掘中发现的鼠骨及相关环境证据，显示鼠类在岛上生态变化中的重要角色。

• 其他考古学家可能对Hunt的结论持不同意见，认为人类活动仍然是主要的环境破坏因素，强调人类社会内部冲突和资源过度消耗对环境的影响。

总结：评论主要围绕波利尼西亚居民到达复活节岛的时间及其对环境影响的不同观点展开，焦点在于人类和鼠类在岛上生态退化中的相对作用。Hunt的理论强调了鼠类在加速环境破坏中的重要性，挑战了传统上以人类活动为中心的解释。

Marae with ahu (a central stone platform) on Mo’orea, Windward. Credit:
Antiquity
Archaeologists have analyzed ritual spaces and monumental structures across Polynesia, questioning the idea that Rapa Nui (Easter Island) developed in isolation following its initial settlement.
The first people in Polynesia settled the islands from west to east, rapidly expanding from Tonga and Samoa across the sea to central East Polynesia and from there to distant lands such as Hawai'i, Rapa Nui and Aotearoa/New Zealand.
After this initial colonization, it was thought that the islands of East Polynesia, particularly the remote Rapa Nui, remained isolated from the wider Pacific world. However, despite their remoteness, similar ritual practices and monumental structures have been observed in East Polynesia.
One such example is the construction of marae. These rectangular clearings were communal ritual spaces that, in some places, remain sacred to this day. However, they changed over time on different islands: on Rapa Nui, the famous moai sculptures were constructed and placed on the ritual temple platforms within marae.
To re-assess how ritual expression spread and developed throughout the region, Professors Paul Wallin and Helene Martinsson-Wallin from Uppsala University compared
archaeological data
and
radiocarbon dates
from settlements, ritual spaces and monuments across East Polynesia. Their results are published in the journal
Antiquity
.
"The migration process from West Polynesian core areas such as Tonga and Samoa to East Polynesia is not disputed here," say the authors. "Still, the static west-to-east colonization and dispersal suggested for East Polynesia and the idea that Rapa Nui was only colonized once in the past and developed in isolation is challenged."
Early ritual structure with pavement and platform at Ahu Nau Nau, Anakena, on Rapa Nui. Above it is the rebuilt elaborated ahu with moai statues. Credit: A. Skjölsvold,
Antiquity
The authors identified three separate phases of ritual activity in East Polynesia. The first reflects the west-to-east expansion, during which ritual activity was focused on actions such as burials and feasting. These sites were indicated by stone uprights. These activities were formed through continuous contact within interaction networks.
The second phase saw the clearer materialization of ritual through the construction of marae. Radiocarbon dates suggest that this idea to make ritual places more visible originated on Rapa Nui, then spread west back into central East Polynesia through existing exchange networks.
Finally, the third phase was defined by increased isolation, leading to internal changes. As hierarchical social structures developed independently in Rapa Nui, Tahiti, Hawai'i etc., large, monumental structures were built to display power.
"The most important finding is that, based on C-14 dating, we can observe an initial west-to-east spread of ritual ideas," states Professor Wallin. "However, the complex, unified ritual spaces (known as marae) show earlier dates in the east."
Overall, while the findings do not question the idea that Polynesia was peopled from west to east, they do show how subsequent ritual developments were much more complex than previously thought.
This indicates interaction networks between islands were robust and, importantly, new ideas were also transferred from east to west.
"This paper challenges commonly accepted ideas about the movement and development of ritual temple sites in East Polynesia," concludes Professor Wallin. "The findings suggest a more complex pattern than previously thought. Initially, it has been shown that ritual ideas spread from west to east. Later, more elaborate temple structures developed on Easter Island, which then influenced other parts of East Polynesia in an east-to-west movement."

Antiquity
(2025).

Fixing underground water pipes usually means digging up roads and sidewalks — a process that's disruptive and expensive. However, researchers at the University of Sheffield in the U.K. are working on a different approach. They've developed small robots called "Pipebots" that can travel inside water pipes to find and potentially repair leaks, all without any excavation.

Pipebot in various environments.
(University of Sheffield)
Old leaky underground pipes are causing a crisis
The U.K. has some of the oldest water systems in the world, with parts of the network still dating back to the Victorian era. Not surprisingly, many of these pipes are leaking, wasting about 790 million gallons of water every day. Fixing them usually means digging up streets, which causes major disruption and adds to the country's $5 billion a year maintenance costs.
A prototype of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Little robots come to the rescue
Pipebots are tiny, high-tech helpers designed to navigate the underground world of water pipes. Each one comes with acoustic sensors, cameras, and rugged wheels that help it move through tight, twisty spaces-while smart enough to steer clear of off-limits areas.
They're dropped into the water system through hydrants and travel in groups, scanning the inside of pipes for even the smallest cracks. When they spot a problem, they send the details back to engineers above ground, making it easier to fix issues without digging anything up.
An illustration showing that a Pipebot has found a leak.
(University of Sheffield)
The robots are part of a bigger innovation plan
These robots are part of a larger effort to modernize how the U.K. manages its aging water infrastructure. The initiative isn't just a university research project-it's supported by the U.K.'s water regulator, OFWAT (the Water Services Regulation Authority), and involves several collaborative projects.
One of these projects focuses on using Pipebots to inspect live, pressurized wastewater pipes, also known as raising mains. The goal is to catch problems early and make repairs before leaks cause pollution.
Another project, called "no dig leak repair," is working on ways to fix leaks from inside the water mains themselves, completely avoiding the need for disruptive roadwork.
There's also the EU-funded Pipeon Project, which is developing advanced, AI-powered robots that can inspect sewers autonomously, without human guidance.
Image of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Kurt's key takeaways
These little robots could be exactly what countries everywhere need to keep their water systems running smoothly. They have the potential to make maintenance cleaner, more affordable, and way more efficient. That's especially important for developing countries where budgets are tight and infrastructure is aging or incomplete. As the pressure to conserve water grows, tools like Pipebots could make a real difference in helping us manage this vital resource more wisely.

data.title: Is Gemini 2.5 good at bounding boxes?
data.author: simedw
data.article_summary: 文章主要评估了Gemini 2.5 Pro在对象检测任务中的表现，特别是在MS-COCO数据集上的 bounding box 检测能力。结果显示，Gemini 2.5 Pro 的表现与2018年的Yolo V3模型相当。作者通过多种设置（包括有无结构化输出和不同token预算）进行了测试，发现Pro版本优于Flash和Flash-Lite版本，且不使用思考预算时表现更好。整体来看，Gemini 2.5在对象检测上表现尚可，但并未超越传统的CNN模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多模态大语言模型（VLM）在目标检测任务中的表现及相关技术细节，包括其与专门计算机视觉工具的比较、性能差异以及应用场景。

不同观点：
• thegeomaster认为，Google的Gemini模型在边界框检测任务中表现出色，尤其是经过后训练（post-training）后，基础的多模态LLM如果没有这种后训练，性能会差很多。
• fzysingularity指出，大多数VLM在定位任务上表现不佳，即使经过目标检测任务的后训练。不同模型的坐标系不一致，如Gemini和Qwen使用的坐标格式不同，这给新用户带来了困扰。他们选择将目标检测任务交给专门工具，因为像Gemini这样的模型在性能上（mAP 0.34）不如DETR等架构（mAP 0.6）。
• smus的实验表明，Gemini 2.5在零样本（zero-shot）情况下表现良好，但在提供视觉和文本示例后性能下降，说明其在结合额外上下文信息方面存在不足。
• serjester分享了Gemini在PDF边界框任务中的成功应用，认为其在精确检测方面表现突出。
• sly010对LLM如何进行目标检测感到困惑，质疑为何Gemini 2和2.5的视觉能力不同，并期望所有模型都能访问相同的最先进视觉模型。
• chrismorgan质疑所谓“地面真值”（ground truth）的准确性，认为MS-COCO数据集并不完全可靠。
• bee_rider关注功率消耗和注释工作，建议使用Gemini作为注释工具，以节省时间和精力。
• xrendan指出，Gemini在处理未训练过的任务（如PCB原理图）时表现不佳。
• mkagenius分享了他们在Android工具开发中的经验，发现Gemini在规划和查找任务中表现出色，优于其他模型。
• mehulashah在文档分割任务中比较了Gemini与其他现代OCR模型，发现DETR架构模型在性能上更优。
• muxamilian认为Gemini的输出在很多情况下优于COCO的地面真值数据。
• EconomistFar关注在噪声数据集中如何处理边界框质量问题，询问是否依赖人工注释或 clever augmentation。
• aae42建议结合传统计算机视觉技术和多模态LLM，创建一个更强大的视觉语言服务。
• nolok分享了个人使用Gemini的体验，发现其在复杂任务中表现出色，但在简单任务中有时会出错。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到不同模型的坐标系不一致问题，这给实际应用带来了困扰。
• 有对LLM如何进行非文本任务（如目标检测）的机制探讨，以及对模型性能差异的疑惑。
• 对地面真值数据集的可靠性提出质疑，强调了实验和比较的重要性。
• 提出了结合传统计算机视觉技术和LLM的潜在解决方案，以提高整体性能和准确性。

44520292.article_content:
Is Gemini 2.5 good at bounding boxes? Sort of...
July 10, 2025
TL;DR Gemini 2.5 Pro is a decent object detector, matching Yolo V3 from 2018 on MS-COCO val.
Multimodal Large Language Models keep getting better, but are they ready to dethrone CNNs in computer vision tasks like object detection? The allure of skipping dataset collection, annotation, and training is too enticing not to waste a few evenings testing.
I decided to write a small benchmark and check Gemini 2.5 on MS-COCO, focusing on object detection. You can find the code and more results
here
.
Hover or tap to switch between ground truth (green) and Gemini predictions (blue) bounding boxes
Dataset
MS-COCO
is a classic in the object detection world, sure it's a bit dated and the masks/bounding boxes aren't super tight, still, it has a long history and it should be easy to place Gemini among the historical results.
There are 80 classes, from
person
to
toothbrush
. Object boundaries can sometimes be ambiguous, but this tends to even out across the dataset.
The validation set, which you are not supposed to train on, contains 5000 images. However there are no guarantees that Gemini didn't vacuum it up during its training.
COCO sees four cakes, Gemini sees only one
Prompt
I've embedded the list of valid classes from MS-COCO into the prompt, and asked it to follow my JSON output schema. I deliberately avoided explicitly mentioning COCO by name in case Gemini had seen it during training.
Full prompt
Look carefully at this image and detect ALL visible objects, including small ones.
IMPORTANT: Focus on finding as many objects as possible, even if they are small, distant, or partially visible.
Make sure that the bounding box is as tight as possible.
Valid object classes: {class_list}
For each detected object, provide:
-
"label": exact class name from the list above
-
"confidence": how certain you are (0.0 to 1.0)
-
"box_2d": bounding box [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000
-
"mask": binary mask of the object in the image, as a base64 encoded string
Detect everything you can see that matches the valid classes. Don't be conservative - include objects even if you're only moderately confident.
Return as JSON array:
[
{
"label": "person",
"confidence": 0.95,
"box_2d": [100, 200, 300, 400],
"mask": "..."
},
{
"label": "kite",
"confidence": 0.80,
"box_2d": [50, 150, 250, 350],
"mask": "..."
}
]
Confidence is important for calculating the Average Precision (see Measure section), however, from experience and some sampling the output only partially correlates with better matches.
I ran this prompt with and without structured output, and to burn a bit more credits I also tried both with and without a thinking budget (1024 tokens). For Pro, a thinking budget of *128 tokens is the minimum, I also tried with 2048 tokens. The Gemini documentation recommends to turn it off, and looking at the result that seems like sound advice.
Initially, I wrote 1024 tokens, but it was pointed out that the minimum is in fact 128. I have updated the results table, but it didn't change the overall outcome.
Measure
In object detection, mAP (mean Average Precision) is essentially the average precision of the model's predictions across multiple overlap thresholds (Intersection over Union - IoU), typically ranging from 0.5 to 0.95. Higher values are better. The goal here is to collapse a graph showing how precision changes as recall changes into a single number, since it's much easier to benchmark with a single number.
Here is some pseudo code, not sure if it makes things any clearer, there are also a lot of guides floating around for mAP with nice illustrations:

• nolok分享了个人使用Gemini的体验，发现其在复杂任务中表现出色，但在简单任务中有时会出错。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flix 语言的特性、优点、缺点以及与其他语言和生态系统（如JVM、Haskell、Scala等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flix 的优点和独特性**：exceptione 对 Flix 语言的代数数据类型、逻辑编程、可变性等特性印象深刻，尤其赞赏其单个可执行文件集成了包管理器、语言服务器协议（LSP）和编译器。他还提到 Flix 在与 JVM 生态系统（如 Java）集成方面的潜力，尽管存在类型擦除问题，但通过 "regions" 概念支持命令式交互。

• **记录的多态性语义**：Joker_vD 关注 Flix 的记录扩展和限制的多态性语义，认为其遵循 Leijen 的方法，允许记录字段的重加和移除，且行为合理。相比之下，早期尝试通过复杂的类型系统静态禁止这种行为显得不必要。

• **语法问题**：daxfohl 对 Flix 语法中的分号使用提出批评，特别是在 `yield` 示例中，最后一行没有 "return" 导致不对称感。他表示可以接受大括号或缩进，但分号必须去掉。

• **Flix 与 Java 的比较和教学**：lutzh 提到曾写过一篇 "Flix for Java Programmers" 的文章，认为 Flix 对于 Java 程序员来说非常有趣，但需要更新以反映 Flix 的最新发展。

• **Aarhus 作为编程语言研究重镇的原因**：textlapse 提出一个题外问题，探讨丹麦奥胡斯大学/科技中心为何成为编程语言研究的强大中心，涉及 C++、C#、Typescript、Dart 等语言的根源。

• **类型类和宏的支持**：pshirshov 关注 Flix 是否支持高阶类型（HKTs）和类型类（在 Flix 中称为 traits）。他对缺乏标称继承表示失望，认为这使得某些有用的抽象无法实现或变得丑陋。

• **代码智能工具的支持**：daxfohl 幽默地提到，是否需要依赖代码智能工具，还是需要自己动脑。同时担心 LLMs 可能会抑制新语言的采用。

• **对 Flix 的兴趣和使用意愿**：andoando 表达了对 Flix 的喜爱，这是他第一次看到新编程语言演示后产生使用欲望。voat 则表示尽管 Flix 看起来很美，但自己是 Web 开发者，从不接触 JVM 生态系统。

• **效果导向编程的介绍需求**：mcdow 请求关于效果导向编程的具体介绍和使用示例。

• **与其他语言的比较**：syhol 指出 Flix 与 Koka 语言非常相似，并希望这些效果系统能够成为主流。Hashex129542 则简单地表示不喜欢过多的关键字。

• **模式匹配的语法建议**：pmontra 对比了 Flix 和 Elixir 的模式匹配语法，建议 Flix 可以更简洁、更 DRY（不重复自己），并提出结构化模式匹配的概念。

• **查询语法的顺序问题**：naasking 对 Flix 查询语句中 `select` 的位置提出异议，认为应该像 LINQ 那样将 `select` 放在最后，以避免 SQL 中的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的 Flix 文档和外部资源链接（如 lutzh 的文章、Flix 官方文档中的 JVM 互操作性说明）为深入了解 Flix 提供了参考。
• 对 LLMs 可能抑制新语言采用的担忧，以及对编程语言设计中语法和语义的细节讨论，也体现了开发者社区对语言易用性和生产力的关注。

Exhibitions
news
Executed Chinese prisoners likely used in UK exhibition
Cadavers on display in 'Real Bodies' show were provided by Dalian-based firm known to have acquired corpses from police
Cristina Ruiz
25 January 2021
Share
The bodies in the exhibition have been stripped of their skin and dissected to reveal their internal anatomy
© jacquemart
An exhibition of preserved human corpses in Birmingham may have included political prisoners executed in China, according to British parliamentarians.
Speaking in the House of Lords on 12 January, Lord Alton of Liverpool said that the cadavers used in an international touring show called Real Bodies, which was seen at the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham in 2018, “were probably people who had been executed” in China.
The bodies on display were stripped of their skin, dissected to show a part of their internal anatomy and then infused with plastic, which gradually hardened, a process known as plastination.
They were obtained from a firm in Dalian, China which has used corpses acquired from the Chinese police, according to a previous investigation by the New York Attorney General’s Office.
The exhibition was discussed during a debate on a proposed amendment to a new British law which is currently under consideration, the Medicines and Medical Devices Bill. The amendment would require all human tissues and cells imported into Britain for medical or scientific purposes to be fully documented with evidence that they were obtained with the consent of the donor.
The amendment is the first legislative response in Britain to the findings of the China Tribunal, an independent panel set up in London to investigate evidence that the Chinese state is removing organs from prisoners while they are still alive as part of a lucrative black-market trade in organ transplants.
Real Bodies: The Exhibition travelled to the South Florida Science Center and Aquarium in 2020
© Photo by Damon Higgins/USA Today Network/Sipa USA.
In June 2019, the tribunal concluded that “forced organ harvesting has been committed for years throughout China on a significant scale” and that “Falun Gong practitioners have been one—and probably the main—source of organ supply”, adding that evidence of forced organ harvesting of the persecuted Uyghur population may yet emerge.
“It is extraordinary that such things can happen in the 21st century, but they are happening,” Lord Alton told the House of Lords on 12 January. “It is crucial that we discover the origins of the bodies that are used in these sorts of exhibitions, which I personally believe should be prohibited in their entirety. The idea that they can be paraded for macabre purposes should fill people with a sense of disgust.”
Real Bodies
is organised by Imagine Exhibitions, a US firm based in Atlanta, Georgia. According to the firm’s website, the show has “recently been updated with the latest scientific research on how Covid-19 impacts the human body”. It is available for hire internationally as a pre-packaged show.
The company did not respond to a request for comment.
However, in an earlier debate in the House of Lords last October, Lord Alton noted that “in 2018, we pointed out that the US organisers, Imagine Exhibitions, were unable to provide any evidence of consent for the use of these cadavers. The organisers merely said that the cadavers were unclaimed bodies obtained from Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company China. Imagine Exhibitions CEO, Tom Zaller, admitted in an interview that the bodies were ‘absolutely from China’ but added that there was ‘no documentation’ to prove their identities or to show they had agreed in life to donate their corpses in death.”
According to Imagine Exhibitions’ website, from 1999 to 2009 Zaller worked at Premier Exhibitions, another US firm which organised touring shows of plastinated bodies. In 2008, the then Attorney General of New York, Andrew Cuomo, reached a settlement with Premier which “brings an end to Premier’s practice of using bodies of undocumented origins in their exhibitions”, according to a press release issued on 29 May 2008. For future shows in the state, the company would be required to “obtain documentation demonstrating the cause of death and origins of the cadavers and body parts it displays as well as proof that the decedent consented to the use of his or her remains in such a manner”.
The press release noted that all of the corpses included in a version of the show then on display at New York City’s South Street Seaport were licensed by Premier Exhibitions from the Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company which, in turn, had “acquired [them] indirectly from the Chinese Bureau of Police”. The company was, the press release continued, “unable to demonstrate the cause of death or the origin of the decedents”.

data.title: Could a Paper Plane Thrown from the ISS Survive the Flight?
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了从国际空间站投掷纸飞机的可能性及其飞行 dynamics。作者Maximilien Berthet和Kojiro Suzuki通过软件模拟和风洞实验研究了纸飞机从400公里高度（ISS轨道高度）以7800米/秒速度投掷后的表现。模拟显示，纸飞机在前3.5天能保持稳定，但由于低弹道系数，下降至120公里高度时，因空气密度增加而失控翻滚。风洞实验中，纸飞机在承受7秒高超音速风（马赫7）后，虽然机头弯曲并出现烧焦迹象，但未解体。实验证明纸飞机无法完整返回地面，但这种设计启发未来可用于如金星探测等任务中的一次性探测器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纸飞机从低地球轨道（LEO）再入大气层时的行为和物理特性

不同观点：
• **nickparker**：认为文章没有覆盖实际结论，强调了模拟与实验研究的主要发现，包括轨道衰减速度、姿态稳定性以及再入大气层时的严重加热问题，可能导致燃烧或热解。
• **peterlk**：同意纸飞机很可能在大气层中燃烧，引用了原始论文支持这个观点。
• **ngriffiths**：质疑文章没有明确说明纸飞机从放置到开始下降的过程，强调了纸飞机由于低弹道系数快速脱轨的特点，并与国际空间站（ISS）的轨道衰减做了对比。
• **fainpul**：认为风洞测试条件与实际大气条件有很大不同，提出纸飞机质量小，可能无法产生足够的热量导致严重加热，并认为即使纸飞机开始翻滚，也可能在低空恢复稳定。
• **FiatLuxDave**：通过计算纸飞机的初始动能和预期加热功率，质疑加热效应的合理性。
• **K0balt**：提出是否存在能够承受这些温度的纸张处理方法或类似材料，比如泡沫隔热材料，但指出这类材料缺少纸飞机的浪漫吸引力。
• **wrp**：直观上认为轻物体由于大帆面积不会经历明显的摩擦加热，质疑纸飞机燃烧的可能性。
• **chris_va**：通过计算黑体辐射功率，指出纸飞机材料无法承受高温，但可能玻璃等材料可以。
• **deadbabe**：提出一个极端假设，使用250英里的电线从地球同步轨道下降，讨论其可行性和摩擦熔化问题。
• **nodesocket**：通过与ChatGPT的后续对话，指出如果飞机由铜或钛制成，由于表面积与质量比不同，其轨道寿命和再入表现会显著不同，强调了弹道系数的关键作用。
• **mcphage**：提出纸直升机的概念，认为它可能比纸飞机更稳定，因为纸直升机会自发旋转。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于纸飞机再入大气层时的加热效应是否会导致其燃烧或热解。
• 不同材料（如铜、钛）的飞机再入表现引发讨论，强调了弹道系数对轨道寿命的影响。
• 提出了纸直升机作为另一种设计方案，可能具有更好的稳定性。

44521094.article_content:
Could a Paper Plane Thrown From The International Space Station Survive The Flight?
Space
10 July 2025
By
Andy Tomaswick, Universe Today
(kieferpix/Getty Images)
Sometimes there are profound questions in life that must be answered, like "What is the meaning of existence?", "Are we alone in the universe?" or "What happens if you throw a paper airplane from the International Space Station?"
Luckily, that third one has finally been answered, because of course someone would eventually.
A new paper
from Maximilien Berthet and Kojiro Suzuki from the University of Tokyo looks at "the dynamics of an origami space plane during Earth atmospheric reentry"
–
in other words, what happens when you throw a paper plane out of the ISS.
First, let's go over some technical ideas that are necessary to understanding this seemingly simple concept.
Related:
ESA Report Says There's Too Much Junk in Earth Orbit Trunk
Origami literally means folded paper in Japanese, and in this case the authors decided to make their paper airplane out of a standard A4 sheet of white paper. The end result looks like something a third grader would have made up to annoy their friend sitting in front of them in class, but with a lot more aerodynamic modeling.
Once the software model was made, it was time to put it to the test. The ISS orbits at around 400 kilometers (about 250 miles), so the authors decided to launch the plane from that height, and at a speed similar to that of the ISS itself - 7800 meters/second.
That speed might seem likely it would shred any plane made out of paper, but at 400 km altitude the atmosphere isn't thick enough to do much damage… yet.
That's actually the case for the majority of the descent back to the ground. From 400 km down to around 120 km altitude, the plane stays relatively stable, given the lack of air.
However, the plane descends very quickly due to its low ballistic coefficient, which is a measure of how well it can overcome air resistance. With its low ballistic coefficient, the plane rapidly slow, descending to 120 km in about 3.5 days.
On the slip side, a low ballistic coefficient would mean that, once the plane entered the atmosphere it would actually have a lower terminal velocity than something like a cannonball.
Illustration of a paper airplane, thrown from orbit. (NASA/ESA/M. Berthet & K Suzuki)
Unfortunately it never makes it that far, as, according to the simulations, at around 120 km altitude, the increased air density induces uncontrollable tumbling, essentially sending the plane into an uncontrollable flight path familiar to anyone who has ever made one of them.
But why stop at simulations when you have a PhD in Aerospace Engineering and can build a paper airplane for science? And why just build one when you can test one in a hyper-advanced wind tunnel on your university's campus?
The answer is you don't stop - which is why the authors built an actual paper airplane model (admittedly with an aluminum tail) and put it into the Kashiwa Hypersonic and High Enthalpy Wind Tunnel at the University of Tokyo to see what kind of aerodynamic forces their paper airplane could withstand.
They didn't go easy on their experiments either. Their one-third model paper airplane was subjected to Mach 7 winds for 7 seconds, similar to the forces experienced during actual reentry. This, unsurprisingly, bent the nose of the paper airplane back, but to its credit it didn't disintegrate – at least not in that amount of time.
There was also noticeable evidence of charring on the nose and wing tips, indicating that, if the experiment had gone on longer, the paper plane would have burnt up.
Ultimately, proving that's what would happen was one of the purposes of this experiment. There are plenty of mission architectures that could potentially use something similar to this paper airplane model – the LEAVES experiment for
Venus
exploration comes to mind, but there are also plenty of Earth observations that would benefit from a lightweight, stable platform to do their collecting from while burning up completely in the atmosphere at their end of life.
Mounting any such mission would require electronics and many other additions that would complicate the purity of testing a simple paper plane that a kid could have made it class.
But sometimes science is as much about inspiration as it is about exploration, and the results in this paper provide a nice mix of both.

• **fainpul**：认为风洞测试条件与实际大气条件有很大不同，提出纸飞机质量小，可能无法产生足够的热量导致严重加热，并认为即使纸飞机开始翻滚，也可能在低空恢复稳定。
• **FiatLuxDave**：通过计算纸飞机的初始动能和预期加热功率，质疑加热效应的合理性。
• **K0balt**：提出是否存在能够承受这些温度的纸张处理方法或类似材料，比如泡沫隔热材料，但指出这类材料缺少纸飞机的浪漫吸引力。
• **wrp**：直观上认为轻物体由于大帆面积不会经历明显的摩擦加热，质疑纸飞机燃烧的可能性。
• **chris_va**：通过计算黑体辐射功率，指出纸飞机材料无法承受高温，但可能玻璃等材料可以。
• **deadbabe**：提出一个极端假设，使用250英里的电线从地球同步轨道下降，讨论其可行性和摩擦熔化问题。
• **nodesocket**：通过与ChatGPT的后续对话，指出如果飞机由铜或钛制成，由于表面积与质量比不同，其轨道寿命和再入表现会显著不同，强调了弹道系数的关键作用。
• **mcphage**：提出纸直升机的概念，认为它可能比纸飞机更稳定，因为纸直升机会自发旋转。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于纸飞机再入大气层时的加热效应是否会导致其燃烧或热解。
• 不同材料（如铜、钛）的飞机再入表现引发讨论，强调了弹道系数对轨道寿命的影响。
• 提出了纸直升机作为另一种设计方案，可能具有更好的稳定性。

data.title: Libpostal: C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: libpostal是一个开源的C语言库，用于解析和规范化全球街道地址。它利用统计自然语言处理（NLP）和开放地理数据，帮助将人类使用的非结构化地址转换为适合机器比较和全文索引的规范化形式。该库支持多种语言，并提供Python、Ruby、Go、Java、PHP和NodeJS的官方语言绑定。虽然libpostal本身不是完整的地理编码器，但可以作为预处理步骤，提高国际地理编码应用的智能性、简化性和一致性。安装过程包括在Mac和Linux系统上通过不同包管理器安装依赖并编译库。项目依赖赞助以持续发展地理空间NLP研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地址解析和标准化库（如libpostal）的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• [支持观点] 一些用户认为libpostal是一个强大且有用的库，能够在处理全球地址解析时提供良好性能，优于正则表达式，并且在多个项目中取得了成功。例如，[Ameo]和[alganet]提到libpostal在解析地址时表现出色，能够有效处理许多极端情况，且易于集成到不同语言的项目中。

• [质疑观点] 部分用户对地址解析库的有效性提出质疑，认为地址本质上是无结构的数据，无法通过解析或标准化来验证其有效性。例如，[kerkeslager]认为，唯一可靠的验证方法是将地址与全球地址数据集进行对比，而不是依赖解析库。此外，[shakna]通过分享自己在非正式地址系统中的实际经历，说明了在某些地区地址的非标准化程度极高，解析库可能无法处理。

• [技术细节和挑战] 一些用户讨论了地址解析的技术挑战和系统要求。例如，[jandrese]指出全球地址格式和惯例的多样性使得地址验证成为一个几乎无法解决的问题。同时，[claytongulick]提到libpostal虽然功能强大，但并非轻量级工具，需要大量的存储空间和运行时资源。

• [替代方案] 部分用户提到使用商业服务或其它库来进行地址和电话号码的验证与标准化。例如，[weinzierl]提到Google的libphonenumber库，并指出许多公司使用商业服务来处理这些任务。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了他们在实际项目中使用地址解析库的经验和挑战，例如[ttw44]在初学Web开发时遇到的困难，以及[RobinL]对libpostal在特定应用（如地址匹配）中局限性的分析。

• 还有用户提到相关项目和工具，如[gorgoiler]列举了一些用于处理日常事物的编码工具，显示出对这类工具的广泛兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 地址解析库（如libpostal）在处理全球多样化地址格式时的有效性和实用性，以及是否存在更好的替代方案（如基于全球地址数据集的搜索引擎）。

libpostal: international street address NLP
libpostal is a C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world using statistical NLP and open data. The goal of this project is to understand location-based strings in every language, everywhere. For a more comprehensive overview of the research behind libpostal, be sure to check out the (lengthy) introductory blog posts:
Original post
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap
Follow-up for 1.0 release
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap: Part 2

Addresses and the locations they represent are essential for any application dealing with maps (place search, transportation, on-demand/delivery services, check-ins, reviews). Yet even the simplest addresses are packed with local conventions, abbreviations and context, making them difficult to index/query effectively with traditional full-text search engines. This library helps convert the free-form addresses that humans use into clean normalized forms suitable for machine comparison and full-text indexing. Though libpostal is not itself a full geocoder, it can be used as a preprocessing step to make any geocoding application smarter, simpler, and more consistent internationally.

The core library is written in pure C. Language bindings for
Python
,
Ruby
,
Go
,
Java
,
PHP
, and
NodeJS
are officially supported and it's easy to write bindings in other languages.
Sponsors
If your company is using libpostal, consider asking your organization to sponsor the project. Interpreting what humans mean when they refer to locations is far from a solved problem, and sponsorships help us pursue new frontiers in geospatial NLP. As a sponsor, your company logo will appear prominently on the Github repo page along with a link to your site.
Sponsorship info
Backers
Individual users can also help support open geo NLP research by making a monthly donation:
Installation (Mac/Linux)
Before you install, make sure you have the following prerequisites:
On Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y curl build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
On CentOS/RHEL
sudo yum install curl autoconf automake libtool pkgconfig
On macOS
Install with one command via
MacPorts
:
port install libpostal
Or as follows with
Homebrew
:
brew install curl autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
Then to install the C library:
If you're using an M1 Mac, add
--disable-sse2
to the
./configure
command. This will result in poorer performance but the build will succeed.
git clone https://github.com/openvenues/libpostal
cd libpostal
# skip if installing for the first time
make distclean
./bootstrap.sh
# omit --datadir flag to install data in current directory
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
make -j4
# For Intel/AMD processors and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
# For Apple / ARM cpus and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] --disable-sse2
# For the improved Senzing model:
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] MODEL=senzing
make -j8
sudo make install
# On Linux it's probably a good idea to run
sudo ldconfig
libpostal has support for pkg-config, so you can use the pkg-config to print the flags needed to link your program against it:
pkg-config --cflags libpostal         # print compiler flags
pkg-config --libs libpostal           # print linker flags
pkg-config --cflags --l

data.title: IKEA ditches Zigbee for Thread going all in on Matter smart homes
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 宜家计划推出20多款Matter-over-Thread设备，以使其智能家居产品更简单、更便宜。公司将通过更新其Dirigera智能家居枢纽，增加Matter控制器功能并激活Thread无线电，支持新产品及与其他品牌设备的兼容。宜家还将重启其音频产品线，推出价格低廉的蓝牙音箱，如Nattbad和Blomprakt。新产品包括智能灯、传感器、遥控器等，逐步取代现有的Zigbee设备。此次更新使Dirigera枢纽成为Matter控制器和Thread边界路由器，未来将支持更多设备类型。宜家致力于通过Matter标准实现智能家居的开放性和即插即用，同时保持价格亲民。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IKEA从Zigbee转向Thread和Matter协议引发的争议和讨论

不同观点：
• WhyNotHugo认为，Matter是一个封闭的生态系统，依赖于公钥基础设施（PKI）和设备证明证书，且Thread需要支付专利费，这与IKEA声称的“更开放的生态系统”相矛盾。此外，这种转换导致与现有Zigbee硬件的不兼容，用户可能需要更换所有设备或面对网络碎片化的问题。

• gorgoiler最初对这一变化感到担忧，但认为Thread通过网格网络支持IPv6，有可能解决Zigbee和IP网络在同一环境下的竞争问题。他分享了自己使用Home Assistant和Zigbee设备的积极体验，并希望Matter/Thread能带来更开放和便捷的未来。

• nick__m质疑Thread相较于Zigbee的优势，认为Thread仍需要一个边界网关，这与Zigbee所需的无线电差别不大。他质疑为什么制造商不继续支持Zigbee，而是转向Thread。

• AndrewDucker希望Matter/Thread能解决当前智能家居设备之间的互操作性问题，特别是Google和Amazon对通用开关的支持不足问题。他认为这将使设备设置更加简便。

• whitehexagon对IKEA放弃Zigbee产品线感到遗憾，他认为Zigbee已经很好地满足了家庭自动化的需求，并质疑为什么需要新的标准。他表示这是他最后一次投资新的家庭自动化技术。

Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
is a smart home reporter who’s been testing connected gadgets since 2013. Previously a contributor to Wirecutter, Wired, Dwell, and US News.
Ikea is relaunching its
smart home line
in a move that will make its low-cost products work with other brands, with or without Ikea’s own hub. Starting in January, the Swedish furniture giant will release more than 20 new
Matter-over-Thread
smart lights, sensors, and remotes with “more new product types and form factors to come,” David Granath of Ikea of Sweden, tells
The Verge
in an exclusive interview.
Ikea is also
rebooting its audio offerings
as it seeks to fill the
Sonos Symfonisk-shaped hole
on its shelves. The first two models in the new line of inexpensive, easy-to-use Bluetooth speakers for the home are the
$50 retro-style Nattbad
and a speaker-slash-table-lamp, the Blomprakt, coming in October, with many more on the way.
Related
Ikea’s latest speaker lamp ditches Sonos for Spotify and inexpensive Bluetooth
What is Thread and how will it help your smart home?
Matter will be better in 2025 — say the people who make it
These new products are part of the company’s ongoing effort to make its smart home as simple and affordable for as many people as possible. “A couple of years ago, we made some strategic decisions about how to move on with the smart range and the speaker range and make an impact in an Ikea way for the many people,” says Granath. He points to the company’s learnings from working with Zigbee and Sonos over the last few years, as well as its involvement in founding and developing the new smart home standard, Matter. “We feel we’ve reached that point. There’s a lot coming, but this is all the first step, getting things in place.”
Last week, Ikea released an update, currently in beta, to its
Dirigera smart home hub
that turns the hub into a
Matter Controller
and activates its long-dormant Thread radio, making it a
Thread border router
. This means it can now connect to and control any compatible Matter device, including those from other brands, and control them in its
Home Smart app
. It will also work with Ikea’s new Matter devices when they arrive, which will eventually replace its
existing Zigbee devices
, says Granath. It’s a major step toward a more open, plug-and-play smart home.
The Blomprakt is an LED table lamp featuring a Bluetooth speaker integrated into its top. It’s part of Ikea’s new focus on smart home and sound as it moves on from Zigbee and Sonos.
Image: Ikea
Initially, Dirigera will only support
Matter device types
that Ikea currently offers — so, no robot vacuums, door locks, or fridges. However, Granath says that as they launch more smart home products, the hub will be updated to support more device types.
The Dirigera hub
already functions as a Matter Bridge
, enabling Zigbee-based Ikea devices to connect to larger
Matter ecosystems
like Apple Home and Amazon Alexa. With the update, it now supports
Matter 1.4
and
Thread 1.4,
enabling energy monitoring and the
ability to join an existing Thread network
, among other features.
While the full rollout is expected later this year, the beta is live now through Ikea’s Home Smart app, but some features will be limited, says Granath.
Matter unlocks interoperability, ease of use, and affordability for us
We don’t have a lot of details on the over 20 new devices coming next year, but Granath confirmed that they are replacing existing functions. So, new
smart bulbs
,
plugs
,
sensors
,
remotes
, buttons, and air-quality devices, including temperature and humidity monitors. They will also come with a new design. Although “not necessarily what’s been leaked,” says Granath, referring to images of the
Bilresa Dual Button
that appeared earlier this year.
He did confirm that some new product categories will arrive in January, with more to follow in April and beyond, including potentially Matter-over-Wi-Fi products. Pricing will be comparable to or lower than that of previous products, which start under $10. “Affordability remains a key priority for us.”
“The premium to make a product smart is not that high anymore, so you can expect new product types and form factors coming,” he says. “Matter unlocks interoperabili

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语音AI解决方案的设置复杂性、实际应用效果、隐私问题、市场潜力及技术比较。

不同观点：
• [mandeepj] 认为现有的语音AI在复杂用例中设置困难，需要数月的时间来调整和监控。他建议利用客户支持电话录音进行训练，并提出通过自测、分析和报告循环来持续改进AI代理。
• [froh42] 分享了个人糟糕的使用体验，指出AI误解词汇和反应缓慢的问题，认为这样的服务不适合公司使用。
• [AndrewKemendo] 对个人使用语音AI处理电话感兴趣，并描述了一个iOS应用的构思，利用真实通话数据进行模型优化，但强调不会分享这些数据。
• [ljclifford] 认为客户支持市场亟待颠覆，对该技术的市场前景表示乐观，并表示有兴趣合作。
• [joelthelion] 对演示表示赞赏，但希望看到实际通话演示以增加可信度。
• [costcopizza] 关注该技术可能导致的就业岗位减少问题。
• [ookblah] 认为演示令人印象深刻，但感觉与机器人对话不够自然，期待未来的改进。
• [ajeet] 对A/B测试和持续改进的观点表示赞同，但指出从测试结果中得出正确结论对利益相关者来说更困难。
• [hajrice] 对需要申请演示而不是直接注册表示不满，并提到申请按钮功能可能存在问题。
• [cootsnuck] 关心该技术的扩展性，询问单个语音代理能处理多少同时通话。
• [koakuma-chan] 询问该技术与livekit的比较，并指出网站上缺乏相关文档。
• [isabelleilyia] 提到在法律领域使用语音AI进行客户接洽的尝试效果不佳，询问其他人是否有类似经验及成功率。
• [shahahmed] 对如何管理评估表示关注。
• [triyambakam] 询问该技术是否与VAPI可比。
• [vinodhkps] 关心反馈循环的形态，以及如何将指标通用化。

补充讨论：
• 隐私问题：[AndrewKemendo] 强调不会分享个人通话数据，显示出对隐私的关注。
• 市场潜力：[ljclifford] 对客户支持市场的潜力表示乐观，并表示有兴趣合作。
• 技术比较：多位评论者（[koakuma-chan], [triyambakam]）提到了与其他技术的比较，显示出对技术优势和差异的关注。
• 实际应用效果：多个评论（[froh42], [ookblah], [isabelleilyia]）提到了实际使用中的问题和改进空间，特别是自然性和成功率。

争议焦点：语音AI的实际效果和隐私问题。部分用户对AI的误解和反应问题表示不满，同时对数据隐私表示关注。
