data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了ACT 2018应用范畴理论研究学校的开放申请信息，并提及了数理科学与几何学的相互联系。文章还概述了一系列关于图解线性代数的博客内容，包括各集主题和研究方向，并邀请读者订阅以获取更新。此外，文章还宣传了对博士生的需求，并提供了其他翻译资源和相关讨论。文章最后列出了一些历史博客条目和其他活动信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图形化表示和简化语言在技术文档中的使用及其效果

不同观点：
• webprofusion认为文档中频繁使用“容易”和“简单”这样的词汇可能会让感到困惑的读者更加沮丧，尤其是当他们还没有理解相关概念时。使用这样的语言可能会适得其反，让读者感到更加无助。此外，作者强调永远不应该在解释文档中使用“显然”这样的词汇，因为如果事情真的显然，读者就不需要阅读解释了。

• AntonioL提到这让他想起牛津大学的Bob Coecke的工作，他提出了量子过程的图形化语言。这表明此类图形化表示在其他学术领域也有应用，并且可能受到先前研究的启发。

• marvinborner指出这些图形与使用对称交互组合子的交互网络中的计算编码有相似之处，并通过lambda演算的例子进行了说明。这表明图形化表示在不同计算理论中具有普遍性和一致性。

• theZilber分享了自己的学习体验，起初认为作者对简单概念的解释过于冗长，但后来意识到这种图形化表示帮助他更好地记住了数学概念及其名称。这表明图形化表示在教育中可能非常有效。

• dtj1123提到这让他想起zx-calculus，这表明zx-calculus和文中的图形化表示可能有相似之处，并且在量子计算等领域有应用。

• Xmd5a讨论了广义Transformer模型，这些模型可以操作函数、图形、概率分布等结构，而不仅限于矩阵和向量。这表明图形化表示在机器学习领域也有应用和探索。

• MarkusQ表示曾经和学生一起关注过这类工作，但感到遗憾的是这项工作似乎已经被放弃。这反映了某些学术研究可能因为各种原因未能持续下去。

• dclowd9901通过引用网络漫画，幽默地指出了人类在匿名情况下的行为倾向，这虽然不是直接讨论技术内容，但反映了网络文化中的某些现象。

• phforms分享了自己多年前阅读相关内容的体验，虽然只读了几章，但这些图形化表示在形式推理中的应用让他大开眼界。这表明图形化表示在学术研究中有启发性和趣味性。

• vismit2000提供了有关沉浸式线性代数的书籍链接，这为读者提供了进一步阅读和探索的资源。

• programjames指出文中的图形化表示与交互组合子有相似之处，并提供了相关链接，这为进一步研究提供了参考。

• lorenzo_medici的评论看似与主题无关，可能是幽默或个人观点的表达。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于使用“容易”和“简单”这样的词汇是否有助于读者理解。webprofusion认为这种语言可能让困惑的读者感到更加沮丧，而theZilber则认为这种图形化表示帮助他更好地理解和记忆数学概念。

• 不同评论提到了多种相关的学术领域和工具，如量子过程的图形化语言、lambda演算、zx-calculus、交互网络和广义Transformer模型，这表明图形化表示在多个领域有应用和探索。

• 一些评论反映了个人学习体验和感受，如theZilber和phforms，他们认为图形化表示在教育中非常有效，并能激发学习兴趣。

• 某些评论提到了相关工作的持续性和发展情况，如MarkusQ提到的工作可能已经被放弃，这反映了学术研究中的一些现实问题。

data.title: Retail cyber attacks: NCA arrest four for attacks on M&S, Co-op and Harrods
data.author: sandwichsphinx
data.article_summary: 英国国家犯罪局（NCA）逮捕了四名涉嫌参与网络攻击的人员，目标包括M&S、Co-op和Harrods等大型零售商。两名19岁男性、一名17岁男性和一名20岁女性在西米德兰兹和伦敦被捕，涉嫌违反《计算机滥用法》、敲诈、洗钱及参与有组织犯罪。所有被捕者的电子设备已被扣押进行数字取证分析。NCA表示，调查仍在继续，将与国内外合作伙伴合作，确保将责任人绳之以法。此次行动得到了西米德兰兹地区有组织犯罪部门和东米德兰兹特别行动部门的支持。受害者应通过政府的网络事件指引网站报告类似事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对青少年黑客行为及公司网络安全问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **公司安全疏忽是主要问题**：[cedws] 认为，尽管事件聚焦在青少年黑客上，但根本问题是公司方面的安全疏忽。
• **系统复杂性导致恢复困难**：[djaychela] 通过其在公司高管朋友的经历说明，现代零售企业的系统高度互联，遭遇网络攻击后恢复正常运作非常困难，给管理层带来巨大压力。
• **黑客年龄引发的感慨**：[gluten_guardian] 对年轻黑客的年龄表示惊讶，认为与自己年轻时的行为相比，现代青少年的犯罪行为更加复杂，并表示希望了解更多关于攻击类型的细节。
• **黑客地域性引发的质疑**：[clort] 对嫌疑人位于英国表示意外，似乎暗示对嫌疑人地域的怀疑。
• **攻击手段的技术细节**：[lyu07282] 提供了具体的技术细节，指出黑客通过伪装成员工并利用帮助台重置密码，进而控制系统并实施勒索，引用了相关技术文章作为来源。
• **访问受限引发的不满**：[casenmgreen] 提到因使用Tor网络导致无法访问相关网站，表达了不满。
• **系统漏洞的责任归属**：[devwastaken] 持激进观点，认为根本不存在“网络犯罪”，问题在于系统设计缺陷。主张要求科技公司对漏洞负责，并提出应由持证工程师开发软件，反对外包和廉价劳动力。
• **怀疑有外部支持**：[aaronrobinson] 怀疑此次攻击背后有外国势力支持，认为仅凭社会工程学难以完成如此复杂的攻击，暗示可能有更大规模的组织参与。

补充讨论：
• **关于攻击手段和责任归属的争议**：评论中既有对黑客具体攻击手段的讨论（如[lyu07282]），也有对系统漏洞责任的激进观点（如[devwastaken]），反映出对网络安全事件中责任归属的不同看法。
• **地域和外部支持的质疑**：[clort] 和 [aaronrobinson] 对黑客的地域和潜在外部支持表示怀疑，反映出对国际网络犯罪复杂性的关注。

Retail cyber attacks: NCA arrest four for attacks on M&S, Co-op and Harrods
Expired
Cybercrime
Four people have been arrested in the UK as part of a National Crime Agency investigation into cyber attacks targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.
Two males aged 19, another aged 17, and a 20-year-old female were apprehended in the West Midlands and London this morning (10 July) on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
All four were arrested at their home addresses and had their electronic devices seized for digital forensic analysis.
They remain in custody for questioning by officers from the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit in relation to the three attacks, which took place in April this year.
Deputy Director Paul Foster, head of the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit, said:
"Since these attacks took place, specialist NCA cybercrime investigators have been working at pace and the investigation remains one of the Agency's highest priorities.
"Today's arrests are a significant step in that investigation but our work continues, alongside partners in the UK and overseas, to ensure those responsible are identified and brought to justice.
"Cyber attacks can be hugely disruptive for businesses and I'd like to thank M&S, Co-op and Harrods for their support to our investigations. Hopefully this signals to future victims the importance of seeking support and engaging with law enforcement as part of the reporting process. The NCA and policing are here to help."
Today's operational activity was supported by officers from the West Midlands Regional Organised Crime Unit and the East Midlands Special Operations Unit.
Victims of cybercrime should use the Government's
Cyber Incident Signposting Site
for direction on which agencies to report an incident to.

data.title: Red Hat Technical Writing Style Guide
data.author: jumpocelot
data.article_summary: 《Red Hat 技术写作风格指南》是红帽公司内部多个团队合作的成果，旨在为技术文档提供写作规范和词语使用建议。该指南涵盖语法（如主动语态、一致性、标点符号使用等）、设计（如标题、界面文档、字体使用）、语言选择（如避免误导性语言、使用包容性语言）、以及如何有效使用交叉引用等内容。此外，指南还包含一个词语使用词典，为技术写作中常见的词汇提供正确用法示例。该文档依据Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported许可证发布，使用时需注明出处并遵循相关商标规定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术写作指南的各个方面，包括其质量、内容准确性、语法问题以及与其他风格指南的比较。

不同观点：
• jonathanlydall认为好的技术写作类似于好的室内设计，只有当写作不好时才会被注意到。好的技术文档应该让读者轻松获取信息，而不被写作本身的问题所干扰。
• azangru对指南中关于连贯句子的例子提出质疑，认为初始版本并非连贯句子，添加逗号只是语调需要，而非语法错误。
• kaycebasques指出技术写作指南常混淆“最佳实践”和“惯例”，前者有实验数据或共识支持，后者仅为保持一致性，建议在讨论时应明确区分。
• hliyana赞赏指南对商业术语的批评，强调语言应明确具体，避免无数据支持的超级形容词和不必要的术语。
• AdmiralAsshat认为指南中混合了基础语法规则和最佳实践，基础语法规则对技术写作人员来说应是基本常识，无需特别说明。
• freedomben对指南的广度和清晰度表示赞赏，认为其对广泛人群有帮助，而不仅限于特定公司员工。
• latexr对指南中关于正确使用语言的部分感到奇怪，质疑是否因常见错误才需要明确规定。
• perching_aix作为英语非母语者，对指南中的例句表示不满，认为某些句子结构和用词不自然。
• jasoneckert幽默地表示对版权声明未使用“Copyleft”一词感到失望。
• phendrenad2询问该指南是否与IBM技术写作指南冲突，并提供链接供参考。
• dctoedt部分赞同指南，但指出某些改进建议可能会丢失原句中的重要隐含信息，对某些读者而言可能有影响。
• dghf质疑指南中关于代词使用的例子，认为应使用“whoever”而非“whomever”。
• dandano认为指南很扎实，并将其加入自己的参考列表，同时也参考其他写作系统如澳大利亚风格手册和Divio文档系统。
• markedathome询问该指南与其他知名公司如IBM、DEC、Sun、Apple、Microsoft等风格指南的比较，指出这些公司均有内部印刷厂和风格指南。
• GLdRH认为指南的某些部分（如4.6节）很荒谬，但可以选择忽略。

补充讨论：
• 技术写作指南中“最佳实践”和“惯例”的区分是重要讨论点，影响指南的实用性和讨论效率。
• 对指南中例句和语法建议的准确性存在争议，特别是英语非母语者的观点。
• 对基础语法规则是否应在技术写作指南中明确规定存在不同看法。
• 对商业术语和超级形容词的批评获得一定认同，强调语言的具体和明确性。
• 与其他知名公司技术写作指南的比较也引起关注，反映出行业内对一致性和实用性的关注。

asyncmcp - Async transport layers for MCP
Overview
A regular MCP Server but working over queues :
queue-based-mcp-example.mov
Quoting from the
official description
:
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs.
But a lot of this context is not always readily available and takes time for the applications to process - think batch processing APIs, webhooks or queues. In these cases with the current transport layers, the MCP server would have to expose a light-weight polling wrapper in the MCP layer to allow waiting and polling for the tasks to be done. Although SSE does provide async functionalities but it comes with caveats.
asyncmcp explores supporting more of the async transport layer implementations for MCP clients and servers, beyond the officially supported stdio and Streamable Http transports.
The whole idea of an
MCP server with async transport layer
is that it doesn't have to respond immediately to any requests. It can choose to direct them to internal queues for processing and the client doesn't have to stick around for the response.
Current capabilities
Transport layer : sns-sqs
Server : Transport layer that listens to a queue for MCP requests and writes the responses to a topic
Client : Transport layer that writes requests to a topic and listens to a queue for responses
Installation and Usage
#
Using uv (recommended)
uv add asyncmcp
#
Using pip
pip install asyncmcp

Note : we don't support FastMCP yet. The examples in this repo uses the
basic way of creating MCP servers and client

Message Size
: For SQS - message size limits are applicable (256KB standard, 2MB extended)
Response Handling
: Async nature means responses may not be immediate
Session Context
: Storage mechanism handled by server application, not transport
Ordering
: Standard SQS doesn't guarantee message ordering

data.title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
data.author: dheerajvs
data.article_summary: 这篇文章报道了一项2025年初关于AI工具对经验丰富的开源开发者生产力影响的研究。通过随机对照试验（RCT），研究者发现使用AI工具的开发者完成任务的时间反而增加了19%。尽管开发者预期AI会提升24%的速度，甚至在实验后仍认为AI帮助提速了20%，但实际结果相反。研究还探讨了可能导致这种减速的五个因素，同时强调该结果仅适用于软件开发领域，并不能广泛推广到其他领域或未来的AI系统。研究旨在帮助理解AI在研发自动化中的影响和风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在软件开发中的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• simonw 认为AI工具（如Cursor）带来的生产力提升具有较高的学习曲线，很多开发者在适应这些工具时反而会降低效率。研究显示，只有少数具有丰富AI工具使用经验的开发者能够显著提升性能。
• noisy_boy 提出可以将AI用作“摩擦消除器”而不是解决方案提供者，利用AI处理小问题如语法，同时保持主动思考，避免技能退化。
• kokanee 指出，评估AI对开发效率的影响很难精确，因为对比无AI参与的任务，AI参与的任务可能在后期产生额外工作量，导致难以准确衡量AI的实际贡献。
• NewsaHackO 质疑研究的资金和发表平台，认为该研究未经过同行评审，且花费较高，质疑其学术价值。
• heisenbit 认为AI可以帮助指出代码中的卫生问题，但也会带来额外的时间消耗，需要区分哪些是暂时性问题，哪些是实际改进。
• fritzo 表示AI帮助其应对快速变化的技术依赖和发布方法，认为AI是拯救开源项目维护者的重要工具。
• 30minAdayHN 分享了个人经验，认为AI帮助其在没有时间的情况下贡献开源项目，但也有一些PR未被接受。
• tcdent 幽默地表示自己已经忘记了如何写代码。
• Jabrov 认为研究样本量太小（16人），希望看到更大规模的研究。
• geerlingguy 表示AI工具在开源项目中增加了不必要的噪音，特别是在代码审查和社区管理方面。
• MYEUHD 提到AI生成的PR浪费了开源开发者的时间。
• nestorD 强调开发者对AI工具的熟悉程度可能影响其使用效率，经常使用AI工具的开发者可能受益更多。

补充讨论：
• 研究样本量小，可能影响结果的普遍性。
• AI工具在不同开发者之间的使用效果差异较大，经验丰富的用户可能获得更大收益。
• AI工具不仅影响个人生产力，还可能对团队协作和项目管理产生影响。
• 对AI工具的实际效果评估存在困难，特别是在长期影响和总体工作量方面。

争议焦点：
• AI工具在开发中的实际效率提升效果存在争议，部分人认为学习曲线高，短期内可能降低效率。
• 对AI工具生成的PR质量和其对开源社区的贡献存在质疑。
• 研究的方法论和样本量受到质疑，影响其结论的可信度。

Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
We conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to understand how early-2025 AI tools affect the productivity of experienced open-source developers working on their own repositories. Surprisingly, we find that when developers use AI tools, they take 19% longer than without—AI makes them slower. We view this result as a snapshot of early-2025 AI capabilities in one relevant setting; as these systems continue to rapidly evolve, we plan on continuing to use this methodology to help estimate AI acceleration from AI R&D automation
1
.
See the
full paper
for more detail.
Motivation
While coding/agentic benchmarks
2
have proven useful for understanding AI capabilities, they typically sacrifice realism for scale and efficiency—the tasks are self-contained, don’t require prior context to understand, and use algorithmic evaluation that doesn’t capture many important capabilities. These properties may lead benchmarks to overestimate AI capabilities. In the other direction, because benchmarks are run without live human interaction, models may fail to complete tasks despite making substantial progress, because of small bottlenecks that a human would fix during real usage. This could cause us to underestimate model capabilities. Broadly, it can be difficult to directly translate benchmark scores to impact in the wild.
One reason we’re interested in evaluating AI’s impact in the wild is to better understand AI’s impact on AI R&D itself, which may pose significant risks. For example, extremely rapid AI progress could lead to breakdowns in oversight or safeguards. Measuring the impact of AI on software developer productivity gives complementary evidence to benchmarks that is informative of AI’s overall impact on AI R&D acceleration.
Methodology
To directly measure the real-world impact of AI tools on software development, we recruited 16 experienced developers from large open-source repositories (averaging 22k+ stars and 1M+ lines of code) that they’ve contributed to for multiple years. Developers provide lists of real issues (246 total) that would be valuable to the repository—bug fixes, features, and refactors that would normally be part of their regular work. Then, we randomly assign each issue to either allow or disallow use of AI while working on the issue. When AI is allowed, developers can use any tools they choose (primarily Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet—frontier models at the time of the study); when disallowed, they work without generative AI assistance. Developers complete these tasks (which average two hours each) while recording their screens, then self-report the total implementation time they needed. We pay developers $150/hr as compensation for their participation in the study.
Core Result
When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts. This gap between perception and reality is striking: developers expected AI to speed them up by 24%, and even after experiencing the slowdown, they still believed AI had sped them up by 20%.
Below, we show the raw average developer forecasted times, and the observed implementation times—we can clearly see that developers take substantially longer when they are allowed to use AI tools.
Given both the importance of understanding AI capabilities/risks, and the diversity of perspectives on these topics, we feel it’s important to forestall potential misunderstandings or over-generalizations of our results. We list claims that we do
not
provide evidence for in Table 2.
We do
not
provide evidence that:
Clarification
AI systems do not currently speed up many or most software developers
We do not claim that our developers or repositories represent a majority or plurality of software development work
AI systems do not speed up individuals or groups in domains other than software development
We only study software development
AI systems in the near future will not speed up developers in our exact setting
Progress is difficult to predict, and there has been substantial AI progress over the past five years
3
There are not ways of using existing AI systems more effectively to achieve positive speedup in our exact setting
Cursor does not sample many tokens from LLMs, it may not use optimal prompting/scaffolding, and domain/repository-specific training/finetuning/few-shot learning could yield positive speedup
Factor Analysis
We investigate 20 potential factors that might explain the slowdown, finding evidence that 5 likely contribute:

44522772.article_summary: 这篇文章报道了一项2025年初关于AI工具对经验丰富的开源开发者生产力影响的研究。通过随机对照试验（RCT），研究者发现使用AI工具的开发者完成任务的时间反而增加了19%。尽管开发者预期AI会提升24%的速度，甚至在实验后仍认为AI帮助提速了20%，但实际结果相反。研究还探讨了可能导致这种减速的五个因素，同时强调该结果仅适用于软件开发领域，并不能广泛推广到其他领域或未来的AI系统。研究旨在帮助理解AI在研发自动化中的影响和风险。
44522772.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在软件开发中的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• simonw 认为AI工具（如Cursor）带来的生产力提升具有较高的学习曲线，很多开发者在适应这些工具时反而会降低效率。研究显示，只有少数具有丰富AI工具使用经验的开发者能够显著提升性能。
• noisy_boy 提出可以将AI用作“摩擦消除器”而不是解决方案提供者，利用AI处理小问题如语法，同时保持主动思考，避免技能退化。
• kokanee 指出，评估AI对开发效率的影响很难精确，因为对比无AI参与的任务，AI参与的任务可能在后期产生额外工作量，导致难以准确衡量AI的实际贡献。
• NewsaHackO 质疑研究的资金和发表平台，认为该研究未经过同行评审，且花费较高，质疑其学术价值。
• heisenbit 认为AI可以帮助指出代码中的卫生问题，但也会带来额外的时间消耗，需要区分哪些是暂时性问题，哪些是实际改进。
• fritzo 表示AI帮助其应对快速变化的技术依赖和发布方法，认为AI是拯救开源项目维护者的重要工具。
• 30minAdayHN 分享了个人经验，认为AI帮助其在没有时间的情况下贡献开源项目，但也有一些PR未被接受。
• tcdent 幽默地表示自己已经忘记了如何写代码。

• nestorD 强调开发者对AI工具的熟悉程度可能影响其使用效率，经常使用AI工具的开发者可能受益更多。

data.title: FOKS: Federated Open Key Service
data.author: ubj
data.article_summary: FOKS（Federated Open Key Service）是一个提供端到端后量子加密的Git托管服务，数据在本地加密后再上传至服务器，确保数据安全。它支持联邦制，用户可以选择自建或托管服务器，并通过现代后量子公钥加密技术防止量子计算攻击。FOKS还提供加密的键值存储，支持存储短字符串或大文件。其团队管理系统允许创建复杂团队结构，支持跨联邦服务器共享加密数据。设备管理功能支持YubiKey，并可在设备丢失时撤销其访问权限。FOKS通过简单的密钥层次结构实现这些功能，使用签名链和Merkle树确保安全性和防篡改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FOKS系统的设计、功能、可用性及其实际应用中的问题和争议。

不同观点：
• **Max（FOKS作者）的观点**：Max强调了在2025年进行基本加密操作所需的“粘合”工作量依然很大。他解释了使用YubiKey进行加密时需要备份和密钥轮换的问题，认为像FOKS这样的系统应当存在，且应是完全开放的，以便在无需支付费用的情况下构建任意应用。

• **WhatIsDukkha的观点**：指出FOKS类似于Keybase的开源版本，并提供了相关博客链接以帮助理解FOKS的背景。

• **xtajv的观点**：对FOKS的名称提出异议，认为其发音容易与不雅词汇混淆，可能会影响项目的接受度和成功。

• **marcopolo的观点**：对FOKS已经支持git功能表示赞赏，特别是可以轻松迁移Keybase git仓库，认为这是项目的一大亮点。

• **hobofan的观点**：认为FOKS项目看起来很酷，且支持无货币化激励的自由系统是有价值的。但从用户角度看，引入该系统可能非常复杂。相比之下，SOPS已经能满足大部分需求，且复杂度较低。

• **aitchnyu的观点**：关注FOKS在分支管理、备份、存储效率及增量同步方面的功能，尤其是对E2EE存储的潜在应用，如密码管理器和笔记应用。

• **pmw的观点**：希望了解FOKS如何促进团队协作，并提出了两个比较：与团队共享的Linux机器和Radicle去中心化git服务，关注点包括联邦特性和数据存储的耦合度。

• **raphinou的观点**：在开放源项目中使用Minisign签名方案遇到密钥更新、撤销和新公钥分发的问题，希望FOKS能提供解决方案，但发现FOKS的例子并不符合其需求。

• **singpolyma3的观点**：询问FOKS的“联邦”机制如何工作，是否数据存储在单个FOKS服务器上，并通过轻量级SSO实现团队成员访问。

• **iovoid的观点**：引用白皮书内容，指出所有管理员必须在同一主服务器上的限制可能是一个重大局限，尤其是在联邦系统中。

• **akoboldfrying的观点**：对“简单密钥层次结构”部分的理解有困难，详细询问了关于基础密钥和用户密钥的加密解密流程，以及密钥轮换的具体操作和成本。

补充讨论：
• **hofrogs的观点**：对FOKS首页使用AI生成图像表示质疑，认为这降低了项目的可信度。

争议焦点：
• FOKS名称的发音可能引发的负面联想，影响项目接受度。
• FOKS系统的复杂性和引入成本与现有解决方案（如SOPS）的比较。
• 密钥轮换和数据重新加密过程的实际操作复杂性和成本。
• FOKS在联邦系统中的局限性，尤其是对多账户管理和服务器耦合度的限制。

44520419.article_content:
FOKS
the Federated Open Key Service (in beta)
What Can FOKS Do For Me?
$
foks
git create secrets
Created: foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
remote add origin foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
push origin main
⏻ Initializing FOKS ... ✅ done
️☝ ️Indexing packfiles ... ✅ done
️⬆️ Pushing objects to remote ... ✅ done
To foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
* [new branch]      main -> main
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Git Hosting
FOKS provides a secure, end-to-end encrypted Git hosting service.
Your data is encrypted on your machine before it is sent to the server,
and the server never sees data or filenames in unencrypted form.
This means that even if the server is compromised, your data is safe.
FOKS is federated, so the git server can be one that
you host, or one that is hosted for you.
Additionally, FOKS uses modern PQ-secure public-key cryptography, so all end-to-end
encrypted data is safe from quantum attacks.
$
foks
kv put /secrets/vitals/ssn 123-45-6789
$
foks
kv get /secrets/vitals/ssn -
123-45-6789
$
foks
kv put -f /secrets/doc.pdf ~/doc.pdf
$
foks
kv get /secrets/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf
$
diff
~/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf && echo "the same"
the same
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Key-Value Store
Internally, FOKS implements git atop an encrypted key-value store.
Clients encrypt keys and values before sending them up to the server,
and decrypt them upon retrieval. You can access
this key-value store directly, which can store either
short strings, or large data files.
$
foks
team list-memberships
owner    devops
member
[email protected]
member
[email protected]
(via
[email protected]
)
$
foks
team list devops
owner    alice
admin    bob
member
[email protected]
member   t:
[email protected]
Federated and Generalized Team Management
FOKS provides a federated and generalized team management system.
You can create teams, add members, and assign roles.
You can also delegate team management to other team members.
Teams can be members of other teams, allowing for complex
team topologies that can mirror real-world organizations.
Morever, teams can cross federated boundaries, allowing
users on different FOKS servers to share data with end-to-end encryption.
$
foks
key list
* laptop 2024-05-04    computer      active
neither 3213         backup        active
YubiKey 5 NFC        yubikey       active
desktop 2023-04-01   computer      revoked
Device Management with Full YubiKey Support
FOKS provides a device management system with full YubiKey support.
You can register your devices with FOKS and manage their access.
You can also revoke access to a device if it is lost or stolen.
Revoking triggers a cascading key-rotation across all teams you are members of,
whether local or federated. This keeps data secure going forward.
How Does It Work?
A Simple Key Hierarchy
To power applications like the Git and KV-Store shown above,
FOKS needs a shared symmetric key for all readers and writers
of the data, available only to the authorized devices, teams
users and keys that the authors specify. FOKS achieves
this natural application requirement with a simple key hierarchy.
Everything starts with base-level keys, like user device keys,
backup keys, or YubiKeys.
Device keys are generated on user devices
and never leave the machine they are generated on. They are protected
locally with system-specific encrypted stores where possible,
and passwords where not. Other base-level keys include backup keys
(for which a human-readable code is the seed), or YubiKeys.
Every user of the system has a sequence of per-user-keys (PUKs)
at the next level up the hierarchy. The secrets seeds for these keys are encrypted
for all available base-level keys. A PUK rotates whenever
a base-level key is removed.
At the next level up there are teams, which work much like users.
All members of the teams share per-team-keys (PTKs), which
are encrypted for the team's members, be they users (via PUKs)
or teams (via recursive PTKs).
Signature Chains
In FOKS, there are two types of
parties
: users and teams.
In both cases, there is a rotating list of constituents (be they
devices or team members), and as these constituents change, so
to does the corresponding active PUK or PTK. As such users and teams
share much protocol design and implementation mechanism.
In both cases, the set of keys that can sign on behalf of
the party changes over time, and it's crucial for security that
there is a careful accounting of these keys that resists
tampering by the FOKS server.
To prevent tampering, FOKS uses "signatures chains", a linear
chain of signatures that can be played back to verify
the ordering of signatures, and that each signature was performed
with a key that was valid at the time of signing.
Merkle Trees
When different parties or computers access keys for a party,
they do so via signature chains; they grab these chains from
the server and play them back to discover the current set of
keys that represent a party.
A compromised server can still cheat here by forking chai

data.title: Perplexity launches Comet, an AI-powered web browser
data.author: gniting
data.article_summary: Perplexity推出了其首款AI驱动的网页浏览器Comet，旨在挑战Google Search，直接吸引用户。Comet initially仅对订阅其200美元月费的Max计划用户和候补名单上的部分邀请用户开放。该浏览器内置Perplexity的AI搜索引擎，默认提供AI生成的搜索结果摘要，并引入Comet Assistant，一个可自动化常规任务的AI助手，如总结邮件、管理标签和网页导航。用户可以通过侧边栏调用Comet Assistant，它能查看网页内容并回答相关问题。尽管市场竞争激烈，Perplexity CEO Srinivas希望Comet能成为用户默认浏览器，从而大幅增加用户请求。尽管AI浏览器是新兴领域，Google等巨头也在朝此方向发展，但Perplexity的早期数据表现良好，显示出一定的潜力。然而，说服用户更换浏览器可能比让他们放弃Google Search更难。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Perplexity推出的Comet浏览器及其定价和隐私问题的不同看法

不同观点：
• 对$200/月的订阅费用表示不满和嘲讽，认为这是高价且不值得的，尤其相比Chrome等其他浏览器，觉得被过度追踪和货币化（whyenot）。
• 提出开放源代码的替代方案，推荐使用本地LLMs和ollama，避免支付高额订阅费（felarof）。
• 对AI公司推出的浏览器缺乏信任，认为这些公司有不尊重用户数据的记录（Havoc）。
• 认为评论中对浏览器价格的批评是误解，澄清浏览器并非仅限于$200/月的用户，其他计划的用户也能获得价值（senko）。
• 对浏览器的功能表示怀疑，认为其主要功能（如主页设置和AI标签）其他浏览器早已具备（glimshe）。
• 认为浏览器的发布并非真正的全面推出，只是针对高价用户的beta测试（GlitchRider47）。

补充讨论：
• 有用户表示一直想要一个有订阅费的浏览器，暗示对收费模式的接受（qoez）。
• 对浏览器名称进行调侃，提出免费的宣传口号（kennywinker）。
• 提及Perplexity可能被苹果收购的传闻，虽然与浏览器本身关系不大，但引发了讨论（freedomben）。
• 有用户质疑浏览器的发布时间，觉得之前已经见过类似的发布（lvl155）。
• 对高价订阅浏览器的隐私问题表示担忧，称之为“隐私噩梦”（symisc_devel）。

争议焦点：
• 浏览器的定价和实际价值之间的矛盾，尤其是针对高价订阅用户的讨论。
• 用户对AI公司保护隐私的信任问题，以及对浏览器功能和发布状态的真实性质疑。

44510913.article_content:
Perplexity on Wednesday launched its first
AI-powered web browser, called Comet
, marking the startup’s latest effort to challenge Google Search as the primary avenue people use to find information online.
At launch,
Comet
will be available first to subscribers of Perplexity’s $200-per-month Max plan, as well as a small group of invitees that signed up to a waitlist.

Comet’s headline feature is Perplexity’s AI search engine, which is pre-installed and set as the default, putting the company’s core product — AI generated summaries of search results — front and center.
Users can also access Comet Assistant, a new AI agent from Perplexity that lives in the web browser and aims to automate routine tasks. Perplexity says the assistant can summarize emails and calendar events, manage tabs, and navigate web pages on behalf of users. Users can access Comet Assistant by opening a sidecar on any web page, which lets the AI agent see what’s on the web page and answer questions about it.

The Search giant has deployed several AI integrations into Chrome
in recent months, not to mention

considered launching its own browser to compete with Google

Comet could get an initial leg up in the browser wars if a meaningful chunk of Perplexity users sign up for the product. Srinivas recently said that Perplexity saw 780 million queries in May 2025, and that the company’s search products are seeing more than 20% growth month-over-month.
Taking on Google Search is no small task, but Perplexity seems to have the right idea by launching a browser of its own. But the startup’s team may find it even harder to convince users to switch browsers than weaning them off Google Search.

data.title: Diffsitter – A Tree-sitter based AST difftool to get meaningful semantic diffs
data.author: mihau
data.article_summary:
**Diffsitter** 是一个基于 **tree-sitter** 的工具，用于生成具有语义意义的代码差异，忽略格式差异（如空格）。它通过比较文件的抽象语法树（AST）而非文本内容来实现这一点。该工具支持多种编程语言，如 Bash、C#、C++、Go、Java、Python、Rust 等。与标准 `diff` 工具不同，diffsitter 能识别出代码结构上的变化，而非仅仅文本格式变化。

用户可以通过配置文件过滤 AST 节点，选择哪些节点参与差异比较。Diffsitter 提供了终端友好的输出格式和详细的日志记录。它支持多种安装方式，包括预编译二进制文件、Cargo、Homebrew、Alpine Linux 和 Docker 等。

示例显示，对于两个 Rust 文件，diffsitter 能准确识别函数内容的增删，而忽略无关紧要的格式变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用TreeSitter等工具进行语义差异比较的工具和方法

不同观点：
• [modderation] 支持使用TreeSitter追踪AST变化，并结合下游代码库的变更进行审查。其工具的最终目标是简化活跃维护的代码库或规范的移植和维护，避免手动追踪每一个上游变更。同时提到手写查询较慢，并对Diffsitter用于展示语义变化表示赞赏。
• [jbellis] 推荐使用更完整和活跃维护的工具GumTreeDiff，并指出语义差异工具在语法无效文件处理上的不足，因此在Brokk项目中选择了传统文本差异比较。
• [ilyagr] 提供了Difftastic等其他工具的链接，并称赞其设计和文档，认为Difftastic也是一个不错的选择。
• [esafak] 提出希望有工具能将大提交拆分为小而具有语义意义的提交，强调对细粒度版本控制的需要。
• [vrm] 认为语义差异与AI模型监督有深层次联系，并提到其团队在编码场景下的相关工作，表达了对不同领域方法的兴趣。
• [jacobr] 提出是否存在一种版本控制系统直接存储AST，让用户获得自己偏好的格式，并允许linters和工具在已解析的树上操作。
• [mertleee] 认为对于更复杂应用，Langium平台和TypeScript比常见AST工具更强大和便捷。

补充讨论：
• [fjfaase] 提到该话题曾在Hacker News上讨论过，提供了链接。
• [1-more] 再次提到Difftastic，并提供支持语言列表的链接。
• [dcre] 提到Mergiraf工具，它使用AST解决部分合并冲突。
• [the__alchemist] 询问是否存在TreeSitter的替代方案。
• [Iwan-Zotow] 关注工具是否能集成到VSCode中。

争议焦点：
• 语义差异工具在处理语法无效文件时的有效性。
• 是否应直接使用AST作为版本控制的基础，以简化开发流程。

其他值得注意的点：
• 多个评论者提供了相关工具和资源的链接，显示出对语义差异工具生态的关注。
• 对不同工具的比较和推荐，体现出社区对实用性和易用性的关注。

diffsitter
Disclaimer
diffsitter
is very much a work in progress and nowhere close to production
ready (yet). Contributions are always welcome!
Summary
diffsitter
creates semantically meaningful diffs that ignore formatting
differences like spacing. It does so by computing a diff on the AST (abstract
syntax tree) of a file rather than computing the diff on the text contents of
the file.
diffsitter
uses the parsers from the
tree-sitter
project to parse
source code. As such, the languages supported by this tool are restricted to the
languages supported by tree-sitter.
diffsitter
supports the following languages:
Bash
C#
C++
CSS
Go
Java
OCaml
PHP
Python
Ruby
Rust
Typescript/TSX
HCL
Examples
Take the following files:
a.rs
fn
main
(
)
{
let
x =
1
;
}
fn
add_one
{
}
b.rs
fn
main
(
)
{
}
fn
addition
(
)
{
}
fn
add_two
(
)
{
}
The standard output from
diff
will get you:
1,2c1,12
< fn main() {
<     let x = 1;
---
> fn
>
>
>
> main
>
> ()
>
> {
> }
>
> fn addition() {
5c15
< fn add_one {
---
> fn add_two() {
You can see that it picks up the formatting differences for the
main
function, even though they aren't semantically different.
Check out the output from
diffsitter
:
test_data/short/rust/a.rs -> test_data/short/rust/b.rs
======================================================
9:
--
+ }
11:
---
+ fn addition() {
1:
--
-     let x = 1;
14:
---
+ fn add_two() {
4:
--
- fn add_one {
Note: the numbers correspond to line numbers from the original files.
You can also filter which tree sitter nodes are considered in the diff through
the config file.
Since it uses the AST to calculate the difference, it knows that the formatting
differences in
main
between the two files isn't a meaningful difference, so
it doesn't show up in the diff.
diffsitter
has some nice (terminal aware) formatting too:
It also has extensive logging if you want to debug or see timing information:
Node filtering
You can filter the nodes that are considered in the diff by setting
include_nodes
or
exclude_nodes
in the config file.
exclude_nodes
always
takes precedence over
include_nodes
, and the type of a node is the
kind
of a tree-sitter node. The
kind
directly corresponds to whatever is reported
by the tree-sitter API, so this example may occasionally go out of date.
This feature currently only applies to leaf nodes, but we could exclude nodes
recursively if there's demand for it.
"input-processing"
:
{
// You can exclude different tree sitter node types - this rule takes precedence over `include_kinds`.
"exclude_kinds"
:
[
"string_content"
]
,
// You can specifically allow only certain tree sitter node types
"include_kinds"
:
[
"method_definition"
]
,
}
Installation
Published binaries
This project uses Github actions to build and publish binaries for each tagged
release. You can download binaries from there if your platform is listed. We
publish
nightly releases
as well as tagged
stable releases
.
Cargo
You can build from source with
cargo
using the following command:
cargo install diffsitter --bin diffsitter
If you want to generate completion files and other assets you can install the
diffsitter_completions
binary with the following command:
cargo install diffsitter --bin diffsitter_completions
Homebrew
You can use my tap to install diffsitter:
brew tap afnanenayet/tap
brew install diffsitter
#
brew install afnanenayet/tap/diffsitter
Arch Linux (AUR)
@samhh has packaged diffsitter for arch on the AUR. Use your favorite AUR
helper to install
diffsitter-bin
.
Alpine Linux
Install package
diffsitter
from the Alpine Linux repositories (on v3.16+ or Edge):
apk add diffsitter
Tree-sitter grammars are packaged separately (search for
tree-sitter-*
).
You can install individual packages you need or the virtual package
tree-sitter-grammars
to install all of them.
Building with Docker
We also provide a Docker image that builds diffsitter using the standard Rust
base image. It separates

data.title: State of the Art: Economic Development Through the Lens of Paintings
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过分析1400年以来的63万幅绘画作品，探讨视觉艺术如何反映其所处的社会经济背景。作者开发了一种学习算法，用于预测每幅绘画传达的九种基本情感，并隔离出同一地点和年份作品共享的情感信号，控制了艺术家、 genre 和时代影响。这些情感分布提供了关于生活水平、不确定性或不平等的细微而重要的信息。文章提出了一种基于情感的测量方法，通过历史艺术作品来审视社会如何经历重大的社会经济转变，包括气候变化、贸易动态、技术变革、知识生产转变以及政治过渡。研究得到了多个机构和项目的支持。

State of the Art: Economic Development Through the Lens of Paintings
Clément Gorin
,

&

Share

DOI
10.3386/w33976
Issue Date
June 2025
This paper analyzes 630,000 paintings from 1400 onward to uncover how visual art reflects its socioeconomic context. We develop a learning algorithm to predict nine basic emotions conveyed in each painting and isolate a context effect—the emotional signal shared across artworks created in the same location and year—controlling for artist, genre, and epoch-specific influences. These emotion distributions encode subtle but meaningful information about the living standards, uncertainty, or inequality characterizing the context in which the artworks were produced. We propose this emotion-based measure, derived from historical artworks, as a novel lens to examine how societies experienced major socioeconomic transformations, including climate variability, trade dynamics, technological change, shifts in knowledge production, and political transitions.

44490321.article_summary: 这篇文章通过分析1400年以来的63万幅绘画作品，探讨视觉艺术如何反映其所处的社会经济背景。作者开发了一种学习算法，用于预测每幅绘画传达的九种基本情感，并隔离出同一地点和年份作品共享的情感信号，控制了艺术家、 genre 和时代影响。这些情感分布提供了关于生活水平、不确定性或不平等的细微而重要的信息。文章提出了一种基于情感的测量方法，通过历史艺术作品来审视社会如何经历重大的社会经济转变，包括气候变化、贸易动态、技术变革、知识生产转变以及政治过渡。研究得到了多个机构和项目的支持。

主要讨论点：潮汐能技术的可行性、成本、环境影响及其与其它可再生能源的比较

不同观点：
• barbegal：指出潮汐涡轮机的维护成本高，尤其相较于太阳能，即使在苏格兰等地，经济性也不如太阳能。
• davedx：认为潮汐能具有商业可行性，尤其是在填补太阳能不足时的能源缺口方面有优势，但其地理限制明显，全球技术潜力仅为海上风电的十分之一。
• KolibriFly：强调海洋环境的严苛性，但对潮汐能基础设施的长期耐用性持乐观态度，认为这可能释放巨大的未开发能源。
• sneilan1：担心提取潮汐能量可能会影响地球自转，虽然作为外行不太了解具体情况，但对此可能性表示好奇。
• edarchis：通过比较法国和韩国的潮汐电站，指出目前试验项目的功率相对较小，但仍有发展潜力。
• NotAnOtter：对在海洋中放置更多技术设备持保留态度，担心设备老化、破损和污染问题，尽管认为潮汐能优于石油能源。
• Cthulhu_：纠正将潮汐涡轮机与陆上风力涡轮机混为一谈的误解，指出海上风力涡轮机也很常见。
• KaiserPro：强调海洋环境的 hostile 特性，包括海水腐蚀性和含沙颗粒的磨蚀性，以及潮汐速度带来的挑战。
• sparsely：指出潮汐能的独特性，因为它既不是来自太阳辐射，也不是核裂变，而是来自地球自转和月球引力的结合。
• sgt101：提到历史悠久的水磨坊仍在运行，显示潮汐能技术的持久性。
• standeven：认为即便潮汐能技术可行，也会面临政治和商业利益的阻挠，如误导信息、政府繁文缛节和关税等问题。
• robotnikman：个人兴趣角度，希望看到水下涡轮机的图片，引发submechanophobia（机械恐惧症）的讨论。
• Animats：指出潮汐能仅在地理条件合适的地方有效，如拥有狭窄出海口的海湾。
• alex_duf：提到苏格兰公司Orbital Marine Energy的浮动设计，强调其简化维护的创新设计。
• worik：提出新西兰关于潮汐能项目的争论，特别关注对渔业和海洋生物的潜在影响，认为需要严肃对待和研究这一问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：潮汐能技术的经济性、地理限制、环境影响（特别是对海洋生物的影响）以及政治和商业阻挠是主要争议点。
• 重要论据：法国和韩国的成功案例、苏格兰的创新设计、历史悠久的水磨坊作为持久性的例子，以及海洋环境的 hostile 特性对设备耐用性的挑战。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：对地球自转可能受到影响的担忧虽然未被深入讨论，但显示出公众对潮汐能长期影响的关注。

data.author: zigrazor
data.article_summary: CXXStateTree 是一个用于 C++20 的头文件唯一依赖的分层状态机库。它具有流畅的构建器 API、基于事件的状态转换、零堆分配的高性能运行时，以及可选的守卫和动作。该库支持 Google Test 集成和代码覆盖率检测，设计上注重可扩展性，未来将支持嵌套状态和 DOT 导出。库的依赖包括 C++20 编译器和 GoogleTest，通过 CMake 进行构建和测试。当前版本提供基本的状态机功能，未来计划增加协程支持和完善的文档。该项目欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个新的C++状态机库的比较与改进建议

不同观点：
• [wangii] 提出该库与现有的Boost-ext/sml库的比较问题，指出sml是最好的或之一，询问新库的区别和优势在哪里。
• [jeffreygoesto] 对README中声明的"零堆分配"提出质疑，指出代码中使用了list、unordered_map和move操作，并建议将与嵌入式无关的功能如导出等分离到另一个库中，以减少小型目标的依赖。
• [baymotion] 提出一个相关的Python库（smax），可能是为使用Python的开发者提供另一个选择或参考。
• [dgan] 对代码中使用"pragma once"表示疑问，指出这通常不被推荐。
• [happyweasel] 简单地建议使用vcpkg来管理该库的安装和使用。

补充讨论：
• 关于"零堆分配"的讨论，[jeffreygoesto]提供了具体的代码细节（list、unordered_map、move）来支持其观点，并提出了对嵌入式开发的实用建议。
• 争议的焦点在于新库与Boost-ext/sml的区别和优势，以及README声明与实际代码实现之间的差异。
• 其他参与者如[baymotion]和[dgan]提供了相关的技术建议和替代方案，但没有深入展开。
• [happyweasel]的评论更像是一个简单的工具使用建议，没有涉及技术细节。

data.title: Analyzing database trends through 1.8M Hacker News headlines
data.author: vercantez
data.article_summary:
本文分析了18年来180万个Hacker News头条，以了解数据库趋势。使用camelAI和ClickHouse数据库，研究了13种数据库引擎的受欢迎程度变化。结果显示：

1. **历史趋势**：PostgreSQL自2020年起主导讨论，MySQL在2012年前占优，MongoDB在2013年达到高峰后下滑。ClickHouse和DuckDB在分析领域迅速崛起。
   
2. **增长最快**：DuckDB增长最快，ClickHouse和Supabase紧随其后。尽管PostgreSQL年对年有所下降，但其3年增长斜率最陡。

3. **衰退引擎**：MongoDB、MySQL、DynamoDB和BigQuery等云原生数据库讨论度大幅下降，主要由于成熟度和开源竞争。

4. **加权参与度**：PostgreSQL在总分和评论数上领先，SQLite平均得分最高，显示其受欢迎程度。Redis引发高兴趣讨论，而BigQuery和DynamoDB评论较少，表明兴趣较被动。

分析揭示了各数据库在开发者社区中的地位变化和趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News 数据库相关讨论中的不同观点和数据分析方法

不同观点：
• codeulike 和 98codes 提到 Microsoft SQL Server 未被提及，暗示可能存在一个在 HN 讨论中被忽略的“企业级”数据库世界。
• xnx 建议使用三个月平均值来减少月度数据的噪音，使趋势更清晰。
• Aachen 询问 MariaDB 是否包含在 MySQL 中，并提出 MySQL 使用量下降可能是因为用户升级和切换到其他数据库。
• Tepix 指出 SQLite 似乎在增长，但在列出的增长数据库中未被提及，表示困惑。
• kwillets 提到 Snowflake 似乎已经达到巅峰，并分享了与 inexperienced devs 打交道的负面经验。

补充讨论：
• vercantez 更新了加权平均分析，将 SQLite 加入增长表，并解释了之前的遗漏。
• zurfer 提供了直到 2022 年的数据概览和其他图表及情感分析，并表示将尝试更新更近的数据。
• Aachen 还提到数据查询工具无法使用，并提出了登录机制的替代建议以避免算法误判。
• nsbk 分享了个人经验，包括从 MongoDB 迁移到 TimescaleDB，并计划用 DuckDB 替代部分或全部 Snowflake 使用。
• 123yawaworht456 询问 HN 故事数据库的下载地址，表示之前的链接失效。
• esafak 关注数据清理方法，询问是否有任何有趣的处理方式。
• bellareed 宣传了他们的免费工具“chat with hacker news”，方便进一步数据挖掘。

争议焦点：
• SQL Server 是否因信号不足或名称问题未被列入分析。
• 数据分析方法的改进，包括是否使用三个月平均值和加权平均分析。
• 具体数据库（如 SQLite 和 Snowflake）的趋势和使用情况的真实性与代表性。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 提供了具体的数据查询和分析示例（如 conradkay 分享的查询）。
• 不同用户对数据库的偏好和迁移经验分享。
• 数据工具的可用性和改进建议。

44496537.article_content:
Back to Articles
Analyzing Database Trends Through 1.8 Million Hacker News Headlines
July 02, 2025
How the analysis was done
I used camelAI with a ClickHouse database of every HN story to do all analysis. You can use it for free with no login
here
to explore the data interactively yourself.
18 years • 1.8 million headlines • 13 database engines
Hacker News is a real-time barometer of developer excitement. I mined every story title from February 2007 to June 2025 and asked three questions:
How has headline volume for each database changed over time?
Which engines are accelerating the fastest right now?
Which ones are losing steam?
1 · Raw popularity through time
The chart below shows monthly headline counts for the eight most-talked-about engines, plus DuckDB (small base, big growth).
Click on the individual database names to toggle their visibility. Double click to isolate a single database.
PostgreSQL’s curve is a near-monotonic climb; by 2020 it dwarfs every other line.
MySQL dominates the pre-2012 era, then flat-lines.
MongoDB peaks around 2013, then slips as SQL engines add JSON support.
ClickHouse (2016) and DuckDB (2020) rocket up in the analytics renaissance.
Redis & SQLite are steady, underscoring their “invisible infrastructure” roles.
2 · Who’s gaining the fastest?

44496537.article_summary:
本文分析了18年来180万个Hacker News头条，以了解数据库趋势。使用camelAI和ClickHouse数据库，研究了13种数据库引擎的受欢迎程度变化。结果显示：

1. **历史趋势**：PostgreSQL自2020年起主导讨论，MySQL在2012年前占优，MongoDB在2013年达到高峰后下滑。ClickHouse和DuckDB在分析领域迅速崛起。
   
2. **增长最快**：DuckDB增长最快，ClickHouse和Supabase紧随其后。尽管PostgreSQL年对年有所下降，但其3年增长斜率最陡。

3. **衰退引擎**：MongoDB、MySQL、DynamoDB和BigQuery等云原生数据库讨论度大幅下降，主要由于成熟度和开源竞争。

4. **加权参与度**：PostgreSQL在总分和评论数上领先，SQLite平均得分最高，显示其受欢迎程度。Redis引发高兴趣讨论，而BigQuery和DynamoDB评论较少，表明兴趣较被动。

分析揭示了各数据库在开发者社区中的地位变化和趋势。
44496537.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News 数据库相关讨论中的不同观点和数据分析方法

不同观点：
• codeulike 和 98codes 提到 Microsoft SQL Server 未被提及，暗示可能存在一个在 HN 讨论中被忽略的“企业级”数据库世界。
• xnx 建议使用三个月平均值来减少月度数据的噪音，使趋势更清晰。
• Aachen 询问 MariaDB 是否包含在 MySQL 中，并提出 MySQL 使用量下降可能是因为用户升级和切换到其他数据库。
• Tepix 指出 SQLite 似乎在增长，但在列出的增长数据库中未被提及，表示困惑。
• kwillets 提到 Snowflake 似乎已经达到巅峰，并分享了与 inexperienced devs 打交道的负面经验。

补充讨论：
• vercantez 更新了加权平均分析，将 SQLite 加入增长表，并解释了之前的遗漏。
• zurfer 提供了直到 2022 年的数据概览和其他图表及情感分析，并表示将尝试更新更近的数据。
• Aachen 还提到数据查询工具无法使用，并提出了登录机制的替代建议以避免算法误判。
• nsbk 分享了个人经验，包括从 MongoDB 迁移到 TimescaleDB，并计划用 DuckDB 替代部分或全部 Snowflake 使用。
• 123yawaworht456 询问 HN 故事数据库的下载地址，表示之前的链接失效。
• esafak 关注数据清理方法，询问是否有任何有趣的处理方式。
• bellareed 宣传了他们的免费工具“chat with hacker news”，方便进一步数据挖掘。

争议焦点：
• SQL Server 是否因信号不足或名称问题未被列入分析。
• 数据分析方法的改进，包括是否使用三个月平均值和加权平均分析。
• 具体数据库（如 SQLite 和 Snowflake）的趋势和使用情况的真实性与代表性。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 提供了具体的数据查询和分析示例（如 conradkay 分享的查询）。
• 不同用户对数据库的偏好和迁移经验分享。
• 数据工具的可用性和改进建议。

data.title: Linda Yaccarino is leaving X
data.author: donohoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X平台（前身为Twitter）的CEO更替及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论认为CEO职位形同虚设，薪酬过高而不值得。例如，[spjt]开玩笑说自己愿意担任一个年薪600万美元的“无所事事”的CEO职位。
• 有人关注新任产品主管Nikita Bier的任命，并提到他与X平台上发布的一个模因可能有关联，暗示公司内部的人事变动。[hakanderyal]
• 对广告平台的批评，[nikolayasdf123]直言ads.x.com是运行广告的最差平台。
• 有人质疑前CEO Linda Yaccarino的实际权力，认为她只是个有名无实的角色。[calmbonsai]、[dekhn]、[eviks]都提到她缺乏实权，许多重要决策都不经她手。

补充讨论：
• 对公司品牌形象的看法，[Hoasi]认为X平台在品牌毁坏的过程中依然屹立不倒，尽管充满争议，但仍然保持了相关性。
• 对旧Twitter时代的怀念，[leakycap]表达了对旧Twitter社群氛围的怀念，认为现在的平台无法复制那种“所有人都在这里”的感觉。
• 对高层人事变动的讽刺，[alganet]将此次CEO更替比喻为“向雨神献祭以祈求好收成”，暗示这种变动可能是徒劳的。
• 关于Linda Yaccarino离职的具体信息，[throwaway150]引用了X上的官方声明链接。
• 对Linda Yaccarino职业前景的推测，[paxys]认为即使回到她以前广告和合作伙伴关系主管的角色，也比继续担任被架空的CEO要好。

争议焦点：
• CEO的实际权力和角色作用：评论中对Linda Yaccarino在X平台的实际影响力存在争议，多数人认为她只是个傀儡，缺乏真正的决策权。
• X平台的品牌和功能变化：有人对平台的变化持负面态度，但也有人认为它依然保持了相关性。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 技术问题，[petemc_]提到在点击链接时收到不当内容警告，虽然与主要讨论点无关，但提出了技术隐患。

整体来看，评论主要围绕X平台高层人事变动及其影响展开，尤其关注前CEO Linda Yaccarino的实际权力和职业前景。

data.title: Anthropic and DeepMind researchers more likely to reject Meta offers than OpenAI
data.author: bhouston
data.article_summary: Meta正通过高薪从其他公司挖角顶尖AI人才，以在AI竞赛中获胜，尤其是针对OpenAI。Meta提供了高达每年100万至140万美元的薪酬包，并从OpenAI、Anthropic、DeepMind和苹果等公司挖走了多名高级研究人员。为了追赶竞争对手，Meta甚至以143亿美元收购了培训数据公司Scale AI的49%股份，并成立新的超级智能实验室。然而，并非所有人都愿意为了高薪放弃工作与生活的平衡。尽管Meta投入巨资，但一些业内人士认为，金钱并非总能打动那些对AI抱有坚定信念的工程师。Meta在AI领域的影响力仍面临挑战，尤其是在其现有技术水平相对落后的情况下。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta是否为AI研究人员提供了高达1亿美元的薪酬 package，以及该传闻的可信度。

不同观点：
• [bowenjin的观点] 对有关Meta提供高达1亿美元薪酬的传闻表示怀疑。他认为Meta不会为个别独立贡献者（ICs）支付比大多数高级副总裁（SVPs）更高的薪酬，这似乎不太可信。

• [bhouston的观点] 引用了TechMeme上的一个简短摘要，指出一些AI研究人员拒绝了Meta的工作机会，选择留在与其价值观一致的岗位上。同时，从Anthropic和DeepMind跳槽到Meta的人数远少于从OpenAI跳槽的人数。这表明Meta可能确实提供了高额薪酬以吸引人才，但并非所有AI研究人员都会为此所动。

补充讨论：
• 传闻的真实性：bowenjin对传闻中的高薪表示质疑，特别是相对于公司内部高层管理人员的薪酬水平。

• 价值观与职业选择：bhouston提到的摘要显示，一些AI研究人员更看重与个人价值观一致的工作环境，而不是单纯的高薪吸引。

• 人才竞争：不同公司之间，尤其是Meta与OpenAI、Anthropic和DeepMind之间，存在激烈的人才争夺，Meta可能通过高薪策略来吸引顶尖AI人才。

争议焦点：Meta是否真的提供了高达1亿美元的薪酬package，以及这种高薪策略是否能有效吸引并留住顶尖AI研究人员。

Meta is trying to win the AI race with money — but not everyone can be bought
﻿Zuckerberg is picking off top talent from across the industry, and OpenAI might be more vulnerable than most.

Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
Month after month, message after message, the AI engineer was hearing from Meta recruiters. The recruiters were pestering him to leave his employer and switch over to support the company’s AI efforts, and they were offering a sizable salary package to do so. But he wasn’t so sure.
The engineer, who works for a startup that was acquired by a leading AI company and requested anonymity from
The Verge
, said he had heard from friends that the company expected a lot of personal sacrifices in exchange for its high salaries, whether on employees’ value systems when it comes to Al or work-life balance. Engineers there, he heard, were working around the clock to catch up with rival companies like OpenAl, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft.
With so many firms desperately scrambling for AI talent, Meta was offering between $1–1.4 million in total annual compensation (which is typically measured as a combination of salary, annual bonus, and amortized stock value) for many AI roles. But, he suspected, its offers might be less generous than they sounded — tied heavily to subjective performance metrics that could be weaponized against employees. And just as importantly, he wasn’t willing to give up a semblance of work-life balance and a healthy work environment to make a few hundred thousand dollars more. He didn’t pursue the opportunity.
In recent months, Meta has launched on an AI hiring spree after making its largest-ever external investment: a
$14.3 billion acquisition
of a 49 percent stake in Scale AI, an
industry giant
that provides training data to fuel the technology of companies like OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta. As part of the deal, Meta spun up a brand-new superintelligence lab led by Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang — and to staff the lab, it started poaching.
Meta has reportedly poached
as many as 10
of OpenAI’s top researchers and model developers, with some pay packages
reportedly
adding up to $300 million over four years, including equity. (Meta disputes this figure.) It’s also approached a slew of other top AI talent across the industry.
Ruoming Pang
, who heads up Apple’s foundation AI models team, reportedly departed for Meta, and at least two Anthropic employees and two DeepMind employees have reportedly joined the team as well. The goal is to secure Meta’s spot in the race to achieve artificial general intelligence, or AGI: a hypothetical AI system that equals or surpasses human cognitive abilities, and the moving target that almost every AI company is currently chasing at breakneck speed. Meta’s primary weapon is vast amounts of money. But some sources across the AI industry question whether that will be enough.
Meta, to date, has not been the most exciting destination for budding AI engineers
Meta, to date, has not been the most exciting destination for budding AI engineers. CEO Mark Zuckerberg has been trying to make up for lost ground in the AI race, having spent years and significant resources over-indexing on the metaverse while competitors like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon invested billions in AI startups and signed cloud contracts and other deals. The company’s Llama AI models often rank low on publicly maintained performance leaderboards; at time of writing, Meta’s first appearance on one such leaderboard,
Chatbot Arena
, was at No. 30. In May, it reportedly
delayed the launch
of its new flagship AI model as developers struggled to deliver performance upgrades, and executives have been public on earnings calls about the need to aggressively invest and shore up against competition. The Scale AI deal, and Meta’s subsequent sky-high budget for hiring AI talent, is Zuckerberg’s Hail Mary: paying a premium for some of the brightest minds in the AI world to safeguard Meta’s future.
But although Meta is plying AI workers with staggering salaries, a mountain of money can’t buy everyone. Anthropic and DeepMind have reportedly had far fewer defections to Meta than OpenAI has, and that’s been an ongoing trend. The reason, to those inside the field, is obvious: the AI world is filled with true believers, and even the biggest companies need more than a cash offer to get many of them on their side.

data.title: LLMs show cultural theory was right about the death of the author
data.author: dcre
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了文化理论中“作者之死”的概念与现代大型语言模型（LLMs）技术的关系。作者亨利·法瑞尔指出，20世纪中期的结构主义和后结构主义理论家如罗曼·雅各布森等人，预见了语言和信息系统的自主性，这与当前LLMs的工作原理不谋而合。尽管文化理论在20世纪末失宠，但其关于语言和文本自主性的观点在AI时代重新焕发了意义。莱夫·韦瑟比的《语言机器》一书试图复兴文化理论，强调其对理解AI技术的适用性。文章认为，要理解生成型AI，需要接受语言创造力与智力可以分离，文本不必指涉现实世界，而是自成一体。文化理论的结构主义理解为现代AI研究提供了重要视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对福柯早期作品的评价及LLM（大型语言模型）技术对结构主义复兴的影响

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为福柯早期作品（如《临床医学的诞生》和《规训与惩罚》）的常见翻译版本读起来令人愉快，但《性经验史》后期的作品由于受德里达影响较多，阅读体验较差。
• PaulHoule表示他一直认为LLM会带来结构主义的复兴，并且这一趋势正在显现。他指出，尽管乔姆斯基的“贫困刺激理论”曾经使“X具有语言结构”的观点受到质疑，但LLM的成功训练表明语言确实具有语言结构，结构主义因此复兴。

补充讨论：
• 对德里达的批评与推荐巴迪乌：PaulHoue批评德里达的同时推荐了巴迪乌，认为巴迪乌在解构文本时表现出极高的精准度，令一些人不满。
• 对乔姆斯基理论的评价：PaulHoue提到乔姆斯基的理论未能成为语言技术的基础，并指出在Zork游戏之后40年，尽管有Inform 7和Attempto Controlled English等技术，乔姆斯基的理论仍然未能在实践中完全实现预期。

争议焦点：
• 对福柯和德里达等后结构主义思想家的评价存在分歧，PaulHoue明显不喜欢德里达，但认可巴迪乌的解构方法。
• 关于乔姆斯基的“贫困刺激理论”是否有效以及LLM的成功是否意味着结构主义复兴，这也是讨论中潜在的争议点。

There’s a great anecdote about Roman Jakobson, the structuralist theorist of language, in Bernard Dionysius Geoghegan’s book,
Code: From Information Theory to French Theory
. For Jakobson, and for other early structuralist and post-structuralist thinkers, language, cybernetic theories of information, and economists’ efforts to understand how the economy worked all went together :
By aligning the refined conceptual systems of interwar Central European thought with the communicationism of midcentury American science, Jakobson envisioned his own particular axis of global fraternity, closely tied to forces of Western capitalist production. (He colorfully illustrated this technoscientific fraternity when he entered a Harvard lecture hall one day to discover that the Russian economist Vassily Leontieff, who had just finished using the room, had left his celebrated account of economic input and output functions on the blackboard. As Jakobson’s students moved to erase the board he declared, “Stop, I will lecture with this scheme.” As he explained, “The problems of output and input in linguistics and economics are exactly the same.”*
Subscribe
If you were around the academy in the 1980s to the early 1990s, as I was, just about, you saw some of the later consequences of this flowering of ambition in a period when cybernetics had been more or less forgotten. “French Theory,” (to use Geoghegan’s language) or Literary Theory, or Cultural Theory, or Critical Theory** enjoyed hegemony across large swathes of the academy. Scholars with recondite and sometimes rebarbative writing styles, such as Jacques Derrida and Michel Foucault, were treated as global celebrities. Revelations about Paul De Man’s sketchy past as a Nazi-fancier were front page news. Capital-T Theory’s techniques for studying and interpreting text were applied to ever more subjects. Could we treat popular culture as a text? Could we so treat capitalism? What, when it came down to it,
wasn’t
text in some way?
And then, for complex reasons, the hegemony shriveled rapidly and collapsed. English departments lost much of their cultural sway, and many scholars retreated from their grand ambitions to explain the world. Some attribute this to the
Sokal hoax
; I imagine the real story was more interesting and complicated, but have never read a good and convincing account of how it all went down.
Leif Weatherby’s new
Language Machines: Cultural AI and the End of Remainder Humanism
is a staggeringly ambitious effort to revive cultural theory, by highlighting its applicability to a technology that is reshaping our world. Crudely simplifying, if you want to look at the world as text; if you want to talk about the death of the author, then just look at how GPT 4.5 and its cousins work. I
once joked
that "LLMs are perfect Derridaeians - “il n'y pas de hors texte” is the most profound rule conditioning their existence.” Weatherby’s book provides evidence that this joke should be taken quite seriously indeed.
As Weatherby suggests, high era cultural theory was
demonstrably right
about the death of the author (or at least; the capacity of semiotic systems to produce written products independent of direct human intentionality). It just came to this conclusion a few decades earlier than it ideally should have. A structuralist understanding of language undercuts not only AI boosters’ claims about intelligent AI agents just around the corner, but the “remainder humanism” of the critics who so vigorously excoriate them. What we need going forward, Weatherby says, is a revival of the art of rhetoric, that would combine some version of cultural studies with cybernetics.
Weatherby’s core claims, then, are that to understand generative AI, we need to accept that linguistic creativity can be completely distinct from intelligence, and also that text does not have to refer to the physical world; it is to some considerable extent its own thing. This
all flows from
Cultural Theory properly understood. Its original goal was, and should have remained, the understanding of language as a system, in something like the way that Jakobson and his colleagues outlined.
Even if cultural theory seems bizarre and incomprehensible to AI engineers, it really shouldn’t. Rather than adapting Leontieff’s diagrams as an alternative illustration of how language works as a system, Weatherby reworks the ideas of Claude Shannon, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts, to provide a different theory of how language maps onto

data.title: Seven Engineers Suspended After $2.3M Bridge Includes 90-Degree Turn
data.author: _sbl_
data.article_summary: 印度博帕尔一座耗资230万美元、长648米的高架桥在中途突然近乎90度转弯，引发广泛关注和批评。该桥本应缓解交通拥堵，但由于设计缺陷，变成了笑柄。七名工程师因此被停职，相关建设公司被列入黑名单。项目设计因公共工程局与铁路部门之间的土地使用冲突多次修改，最终导致不合理转弯。当局正考虑购买更多土地以修正问题，但将导致更多开支和延误。此事成为官僚内斗和妥协设计的警示案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：印度一座桥梁设计多次变更，最终呈现90度转角，引发的讨论涉及工程设计、文化差异、以及对基础设施质量的批评。

不同观点：
• [oc1] 认为印度人在面对工程问题时具有灵活应变的精神，不会直接拒绝项目，而是找到解决办法，类似于软件开发中的思维方式。
• [BitwiseFool] 分享个人经历，提到受游戏影响，曾认为桥梁必须是直的，直到现实中见到弯曲的桥梁，这种体验颠覆了他原有的认知。
• [Aloisius] 指出实际转角并没有90度，而是大约120度，并提供了地图链接以支持其观点。
• [geodel] 批评印度基础设施质量差，并将其与欧美对比，提到印度有两种人：默默忍受不便的多数人和在网上激烈捍卫国家形象的少数人。
• [rilindo] 提供美国芝加哥湖岸S形曲线的例子，暗示类似设计并非印度独有。
• [recursive] 分享本地一个三向桥梁的例子，说明右转角部分仅供行人和自行车使用，认为设计实际上还不错。
• [andysinclair] 提到希腊雅典有一座带有两个90度转角的桥梁，认为设计奇怪。
• [a012] 提到越南也有一个真正的90度桥梁，提供了视频链接。
• [taeric] 表示同情，认为设计可能是受到某些限制所致，但看到实际建成仍然感到震惊。
• [hanlonsrazor] 认为只要桥梁能完成其功能且司机以合理速度驾驶，设计就没有问题，并对工程师团队表示支持。
• [kylehotchkiss] 讽刺地提到承包商可以通过关闭旧公司、开设新公司来解决被列入黑名单的问题。
• [cjcenizal] 调侃工程师选择了错误的转角设计。
• [sys32768] 质疑这些设计者是否真的具备工程师的专业能力，暗示他们可能只是拥有工程学位。
• [FredPret] 提到在老游戏《Stunts》的编辑器中也曾设计过类似桥梁，将讨论带入轻松的游戏话题。
• [general1726] 指出工程师通常不负责高层决策，认为如果下次对结果不满意可以解雇施工人员。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于桥梁设计的合理性以及是否反映了印度基础设施建设的普遍问题。
• 不同用户提供了全球其他地方类似设计的例子，试图淡化对印度的批评或提供对比。
• 讨论中包含了对工程师角色和责任的调侃以及对官僚决策过程的批评。

Ever had to make a 90-degree turn
on a bridge
? No? That’s the problem. In India, seven engineers just got suspended for designing exactly that.
A brand-new $2.3 million bridge in Bhopal, India, is going viral—not because it solved traffic, but because it bends at nearly a 90-degree angle. Now, seven engineers have been suspended, a retired official is facing investigation, and the construction firms behind the project have been blacklisted.
Videos by VICE
The 648-meter Rail Over Bridge (ROB) was supposed to connect Mahamai Ka Bagh and New Bhopal, easing congestion and slashing wait times for up to 300,000 daily commuters. Instead, it’s become a punchline and a cautionary tale.
7 Engineers Suspended Over Bhopal Bridge With 90-Degree Turn
Photos of the sharp turn, which appears midway through the elevated roadway, exploded on Indian social media, prompting disbelief and concern. Drivers expressed confusion about how to navigate the turn safely. Others wondered how the project even got approved.
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav didn’t waste time. “Seven engineers, including two chief engineers, have been suspended with immediate effect,” he said, according to
The Indian Express
. “A departmental inquiry will be conducted against a retired sub-engineer. Both the construction agency and the design consultant have been blacklisted.”
According to official records, the design for the bridge shifted multiple times over the past seven years, largely due to conflicts between the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Railways. The two agencies couldn’t agree on how to share land, and in trying to work around both railway property and the new Metro line, they ended up producing a final layout with an abrupt 90-degree angle.
VD Verma, the project’s chief engineer, defended the layout, saying his team had no other option due to “limited land space” and the proximity of the Metro station. But critics argue that no one should ever have signed off on a turn that sharp.
Internal PWD documents show the original 2018 plan featured a more manageable 45-degree skew. That plan was scrapped after the Railways refused to approve construction on its land. A second design attempted to accommodate the Metro line. A third version adjusted for alignment errors, though the Railways later admitted that the final result “is neither fulfilling the functional requirement nor safe for road users.”
Now, Bhopal authorities are discussing buying additional land to fix the turn, but that means more money and more delays.
For commuters who hoped this project would ease daily travel, the bridge has become yet another example of bureaucratic infighting and design-by-compromise. For engineers, it’s a high-profile reminder that bad geometry can turn into political fallout very quickly.

data.title: Woman and three teenagers arrested over M&S, Co-op and Harrods cyber attacks
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 英国警方逮捕了一名20岁女子和三名青少年，他们涉嫌参与针对M&S、Co-op和Harrods的网络攻击。这四人因涉嫌违反《计算机滥用法》、勒索、洗钱及参与有组织犯罪活动在家中被捕。此次攻击导致M&S线上订单暂停，店铺货架空置，预计将造成高达3亿英镑的损失。Co-op和Harrods也遭到攻击，部分系统被迫关闭。国家犯罪局（NCA）称此次逮捕是调查的“重大进展”，并继续与国内外伙伴合作追查责任人。M&S主席称此次攻击如“灵魂出窍”，但拒绝透露是否支付赎金。警方从嫌疑人处缴获电子设备进行分析。
data.comments_summary:

Woman and three teenagers arrested over M&S, Co-op and Harrods cyber attacks
Disruption from the M&S attack continues and is likely to cost the retailer hundreds of millions of pounds.
Adele Robinson
News correspondent
@SkyNewsAdele
Thursday 10 July 2025 14:01, UK
Image:
A man walks past empty shelves in a branch of the Co-op in Manchester following the major cyber attack. Pic: PA
Why you can trust Sky News
Four people have been arrested by police investigating cyber attacks targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.
A 20-year-old woman and two males, both aged 19, and another aged 17, were detained in London and the West Midlands as part of a National Crime Agency (NCA) operation.
They were arrested at their homes on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
Money blog: Cost of renting over owning home is a lot
Electronic devices were seized from the suspects and are currently being analysed by forensic experts.
M&S
halted online orders
, and shelves were empty in shops after the cyber attack on the retailer earlier this year.

The arrests, which took place early on Thursday morning, were supported by officers from the West Midlands regional organised crime unit and the East Midlands special operations unit.
Earlier this week, the chairman of M&S told MPs that the hack had been "traumatic" and like an "out-of-body experience".
Archie Norman, however,
refused to be drawn
on whether the retailer had paid any ransom.

data.title: Bribe or community benefit? Sweeteners for renewables need to be done right
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了可再生能源项目在社区中引发的反应，特别是如何通过社区利益共享计划来缓解反对意见。这些计划通常包括社区基金、实物福利和本地所有权模式，旨在补偿项目对当地居民的影响，并提升项目的接受度。然而，如果设计不当，这些支付可能被视为贿赂，尤其是当其目的是为了影响社区接受项目时。文章强调，必须精心设计这些计划，以避免引发负面 perception，并指出澳大利亚及全球在风能和太阳能项目中越来越多地采用此类社区受益机制。昆士兰州已立法要求可再生能源开发商与社区签订利益协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社区对基础设施建设（如压裂开采与可再生能源项目）的看法和影响

不同观点：
• 一些社区对被选中建设基础设施（如压裂开采）感到不满，因为尽管部分土地所有者可能获得补偿，但其他受影响的居民却未得到任何赔偿。这导致了不公平感。
  - 例子：有用户提到自己附近的压裂操作不仅没得到补偿，反而面临饮用水污染、地震和地面沉降等问题。

• 部分居民认为可再生能源设施（如太阳能农场和风力涡轮机）比化石燃料开采（如压裂和煤矿）对社区的负面影响更小，且更愿意接受这些绿色能源项目。
  - 例子：该用户明确表示宁愿家旁边是太阳能农场或风力涡轮机，也不希望靠近压裂操作或煤矿。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了化石燃料开采（如压裂）带来的具体问题，包括环境污染（如不安全的饮用水）和地质问题（如地震和地面沉降），这些问题加剧了居民的不满。
• 可再生能源设施被视为化石燃料开采的替代选项，显示了公众对能源项目选择上的偏好变化，以及对绿色能源的支持。
• 争议焦点在于补偿机制的不公平和化石燃料开采对社区造成的负面影响，居民认为双重标准明显，且缺乏有效的补偿或解决方案。

When a renewable energy developer announces a new project, there’s one big question mark – how will nearby communities react?
Community pushback has
scuttled many renewables projects
. Sometimes, communities are angry landowners hosting infrastructure will be paid, but neighbours and those further afield may not.
As a result, renewable projects often involve schemes where the developer gives funding or resources to local community initiatives.
Australia has dozens of these schemes, with many more to come as the clean energy transition accelerates. The Clean Energy Council
estimates
developers contribute about A$1,050 to communities for every megawatt of wind and about $850 for solar.
The problem is,
research shows
poorly designed schemes can look a lot like bribery. Developers dish out money to gain community acceptance. Our
new research
points to a clear solution:
design these schemes carefully
.
How do these schemes work?
Renewable developers usually structure community-benefit schemes in one of three ways:
community funds, where a developer offers a one-time or ongoing payment for local infrastructure such as roads, services or community projects
in-kind benefits, such as investment in local sports fields or tourism initiatives
local ownership models, such as offering community members preferential access to shares in the company or a community co-ownership model of the project.
In Australia, a number of community schemes are already
established
or
planned
.
More are on their way. The Queensland government has
introduced laws
which
require
wind and solar farm developers enter into community benefit agreements.
Worldwide, offshore wind farms have
for many years
involved community benefit sharing. Australia is
very likely
to follow suit as this industry emerges.
Developers will sometimes set up more targeted
neighbour payment
schemes where funding is given to nearby landowners.
What are they for?
There are
three reasons
why benefit sharing can be a good idea overall. They are:
1. Impact on locals:
solar farms take up large areas of land, while wind farms on land or sea draw the eye and
can compete with
other uses of the space. Community benefit schemes can help counterbalance these impacts.
2. Benefits are centralised:
solar, wind and battery developments generate significant
economic value
. But this is largely captured by the developer. Benefit schemes can make residents feel the deal is fairer.
3. Acceptance:
change of any kind is often hard. Offering incentives to towns and communities can make the change easier.
Payments to communities hosting renewable projects can look like bribes if not done carefully.
myphotobank.com.au/Shutterstock
Straying into bribery?
The definition of a
bribe
is a benefit which
influences
or intends to influence a person to violate their role-based obligations. Offering money to a police officer to avoid losing your licence would count as a bribe.
Community benefit sharing isn’t a bribe in a strict legal sense. But the payments can resemble bribes if they influence community members to accept the new development. Improving community acceptance is often a
central goal
of such schemes.
The accusation is common. In the United Kingdom, researchers
observe
these schemes are regularly seen:
as an attempt by local developers to ‘bribe’ local communities to ‘buy’ support for their wind farm development.
Community members may decry a scheme as a “
paltry bribe
” or “
shut up candy
”. Some
insist
their “principles are not for sale”.
Developers recognise this too. As
one says
:
you don’t just turn up in a community and say, don’t worry, we’ll buy you a new rugby pitch […] because it

data.title: Microsoft Touts $500M AI Savings While Slashing Jobs
data.author: Michelangelo11
data.article_summary: 微软公司在内部展示中表示，人工智能（AI）工具正显著提升销售、客服和软件工程等领域的生产力。据首席商务官Judson Althoff透露，AI去年为微软呼叫中心节省超过5亿美元，并提高了员工和客户满意度。AI还被用于处理小客户的互动，已创造数千万美元收入。尽管AI带来效率提升，微软仍宣布裁员约1.5万人，主要集中在销售等客户 facing 岗位。微软强调，AI并非近期裁员的主因，并推出GitHub Copilot等工具帮助员工提高工作效率。科技行业高管普遍认为AI将替代部分人工劳动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI节省成本的说法持不同看法

不同观点：
• [duxup的观点] 对AI节省成本的说法持怀疑态度。duxup指出，经常看到高管做出这样的声明，但缺乏详细的解释或实际调查结果，似乎只是一种必须的表态，而不是基于具体数据或分析。

• [erentz的观点] 根据个人见闻，指出其在微软工作的朋友因为人手不足而感到更加紧张和压力大，需要更加努力工作，而不是因为AI的引入而获得显著的工作效率提升。这表明AI在实际工作环境中可能并没有产生预期中的积极效果。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否真正如高管所声称的那样，带来了显著的工作效率提升和成本节省。duxup质疑这些声明的真实性和详细程度，而erentz通过个人观察提供了与高管声明相矛盾的实际案例。

• 讨论中还涉及了AI在工作场所的实际应用效果，特别是在员工感受和工作压力方面，这可能与高管所宣传的理想效果存在差距。

Brody Ford

2 min read
In This Article:
META
GOOG

MSFT
(Bloomberg) -- Microsoft Corp. is keen to show employees how much AI is transforming its own workplace, even as the company terminates thousands of personnel.
Most Read from Bloomberg

Are Tourists Ruining Europe? How Locals Are Pushing Back
Can Americans Just Stop Building New Highways?

During a presentation this week, Chief Commercial Officer Judson Althoff said artificial intelligence tools are boosting productivity in everything from sales and customer service to software engineering, according to a person familiar with his remarks.
Althoff said AI saved Microsoft more than $500 million last year in its call centers alone and increased both employee and customer satisfaction, according to the person, who requested anonymity to discuss an internal matter.
The company is also starting to use AI to handle interactions with smaller customers, Althoff said. This effort is nascent, but already generating tens of millions of dollars, he said.
Microsoft declined to comment.
Tech executives have been increasingly vocal about the potential for AI to automate labor currently performed by humans. Salesforce Inc. has said 30% of internal work at the company is being handled by AI, allowing it to reduce hiring for some roles. Executives at Alphabet Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. have said significant chunks of code are now being written with AI.
At Microsoft, AI generated 35% of the code for new products, accelerating launch times, Althoff said. The company’s GitHub Copilot is a leader in the market for AI coding tools and has 15 million users, Microsoft said in April.
AI implementation has fueled replacement anxiety for many workers, particularly in the tech industry. Microsoft has announced cuts of about 15,000 employees this year, with a wave of layoffs last week targeting customer-facing roles like sales.
Althoff stressed to employees that AI could make them more effective as sellers. Through the use of Microsoft’s Copilot AI assistant, each salesperson is finding more leads, closing deals quicker and generating 9% more revenue, he said.
Productivity gains from AI were “not a predominant factor” in the job reductions of recent months, Microsoft’s top lawyer Brad Smith said Wednesday during an event announcing a donation of over $4 billion in cash and technology to schools with a focus on spreading AI skills.

If you want
a job at McDonald’s today, there’s a good chance you'll have to talk to Olivia. Olivia is not, in fact, a human being, but instead an
AI chatbot
that screens applicants, asks for their contact information and résumé, directs them to a personality test, and occasionally makes them “
go insane
” by repeatedly misunderstanding their most basic questions.
Until last week, the platform that runs the Olivia chatbot, built by artificial intelligence software firm Paradox.ai, also suffered from absurdly basic security flaws. As a result, virtually any hacker could have accessed the records of every chat Olivia had ever had with McDonald's applicants—including all the personal information they shared in those conversations—with tricks as straightforward as guessing that an administrator account's username and password was “123456."
On Wednesday, security researchers Ian Carroll and Sam Curry
revealed
that they found simple methods to hack into the backend of the AI chatbot platform on McHire.com, McDonald's website that many of its franchisees use to handle job applications. Carroll and Curry, hackers with a
long
track
record
of independent security testing, discovered that simple web-based vulnerabilities—including guessing one laughably weak password—allowed them to access a Paradox.ai account and query the company's databases that held every McHire user's chats with Olivia. The data appears to include as many as 64 million records, including applicants' names, email addresses, and phone numbers.
Carroll says he only discovered that appalling lack of security around applicants' information because he was intrigued by McDonald's decision to subject potential new hires to an AI chatbot screener and personality test. “I just thought it was pretty uniquely dystopian compared to a normal hiring process, right? And that's what made me want to look into it more,” says Carroll. “So I started applying for a job, and then after 30 minutes, we had full access to virtually every application that's ever been made to McDonald's going back years.”
When WIRED reached out to McDonald’s and Paradox.ai for comment, a spokesperson for Paradox.ai shared a
blog post
the company planned to publish that confirmed Carroll and Curry’s findings. The company noted that only a fraction of the records Carroll and Curry accessed contained personal information, and said it had verified that the administrator account with the “123456” password that exposed the information “was not accessed by any third party” other than the researchers. The company also added that it’s instituting a bug bounty program to better catch security vulnerabilities in the future. “We do not take this matter lightly, even though it was resolved swiftly and effectively,” Paradox.ai’s chief legal officer, Stephanie King, told WIRED in an interview. “We own this.”
In its own statement to WIRED, McDonald’s agreed that Paradox.ai was to blame. “We’re disappointed by this unacceptable vulnerability from a third-party provider, Paradox.ai. As soon as we learned of the issue, we mandated Paradox.ai to remediate the issue immediately, and it was resolved on the same day it was reported to us,” the statement reads. “We take our commitment to cyber security seriously and will continue to hold our third-party providers accountable to meeting our standards of data protection.”
One of the exposed interactions between a job applicant and “Olivia.”
Courtesy of Ian Carroll and Sam Curry
Carroll says he became interested in the security of the McHire website after spotting a
Reddit post
complaining about McDonald's hiring chatbot wasting applicants' time with nonsense responses and misunderstandings. He and Curry started talking to the chatbot themselves, testing it for
“prompt injection” vulnerabilities
that can enable someone to hijack a large language model and bypass its safeguards by sending it certain commands. When they couldn't find any such flaws, they decided to see what would happen if they signed up as a McDonald's franchisee to get access to the backend of the site, but instead spotted a curious login link on McHire.com for staff at Paradox.ai, the company that built the site.
On a whim, Carroll says he tried two of the most common sets of login credentials: The username and password “admin," and then the username and password “123456.” The second of those two tries worked. “It's more common than you'd think,” Carroll says. There appeared to be no multifactor authentication for that Paradox.ai login page.
With those credentials, Carroll and Curry could see they now had administrator access to a test McDonald's “restaurant” on McHire, and they figured out all the employees listed there appeared to be Paradox.ai developers, seemingly based in Vietnam. They found a link within the platform to apparent test job postings for that nonexistent McDonald's location, clicked on one posting, applied to it, and could see their own app

data.title: ESIM Security
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了AG Security Research公司下属的Security Explorations研究实验室对eSIM技术的安全性分析。他们成功破解了装有GSMA消费者证书的Kigen eUICC卡，展示了eSIM在安全性上的漏洞。eSIM本应通过GSMA的多层认证机制保护移动网络运营商和用户，但研究表明，攻击者可以通过物理访问和掌握密钥，在eUICC上安装恶意Java应用程序。此次攻击暴露了eSIM在配置文件和Java应用程序上的安全性缺失，且可能通过SMS-PP协议进行远程攻击。该研究验证了2019年关于Java Card的漏洞报告，并呼吁移动运营商和安全公司关注eSIM的安全风险。

In a result of its research investigation efforts, Security Explorations, a research lab of AG Security Research company, conducted security analysis of eSIM technology.
This section of our website presents initial information regarding the project.
Notes
We broke security of
Kigen
(*)
eUICC
card with
GSMA
consumer certificates installed into it.
The eUICC card makes it possible to install the so called eSIM profiles into target chip. eSIM profiles are software representations of mobile subscriptions. For many years such mobile subscriptions had a form of a physical
SIM card
of various factors (SIM, microSIM, nonoSIM). With eSIM, the subscription can come in a pure digital form (as a software bundle), it can also carry Java Card applications.
According to Kigen:
1) eSIMs are "as secure and interoperable as SIM cards [...] thanks to the multi-layered GSMA eSIM certification scheme that protects device makers, device owners and mobile network operators (MNOs)" (
source
)
2) "Kigen OS offers the highest level of logical security when employed on any SIM form factor, including a secure enclave" and "Kigen SIM OS features help differentiate, scale and grow revenues with zero compromise security" (
source
)
The hack proves that our
research on Java Card from 2019
did matter. Oracle indicated the
vulnerabilities we reported
to the company in 2019 were rather irrelevant (the company referred to them as "security concerns") / did not affect their production Java Card VM. These are now proved to be real bugs.
This is likely the first successful public hack against:
consumer GSMA eUICC
Kigen eSIM (Kigen
press releases
and
web pages
implicate over 2 billion SIMs enabled by Kigen secure SIM OS)
EAL(**) certified GSMA security chip (
SLC37 chip
based on 32-bit ARM SecurCore SC300 processor from
Infineon
)
The attack against Kigen eUICC relies both on physical access to sample card along knowledge of the keys used for malicious Java app installation. The remote over-the-air (OTA) vector can't be excluded - our Proof of Concept code mimics a malicious applet installation over OTA
SMS-PP protocol
(Short Message Service Point to Point) on a target Kigen eUICC. In that context, knowledge of the keys is a primary requirement for target card compromise.
The hack proves no security / isolation for the eSIM profile and Java apps (no security for eUICC memory content).
It's worth to note that while this work builds on our past Java Card research from 2019 (along [
25
] [
years
] [
of
] [
Java
] [
hacking
] experience), it required development of some new exploitation techniques / know-how.
We hope the hack brings eSIM security along associated security risks to the focus of mobile network operators (MNOs), vendors, security researchers and security companies. This is important in the context of somewhat bold security claims / overconfidence of eUICC vendors (vide
leaf eUICC cert valid for 100 years
) and MNO assumptions pertaining to profile trust and its storage in a tamper-proof security element (MNO profile integrity / no compromise / no tampering assumed).
(*) as denoted by eUICC / EUM certificates and card EID
(**)
RSP specification
impose minimum EAL4 level ("4.14.1 eUICC Certification Requirements", page 55)
Crypto Proof
As a result of eUICC compromise, we were able to extract private
ECC
key for the certificate

data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 文章报道了在赞比亚一家黑猩猩保护区出现的新奇行为趋势。自2023年8月起，一只名为Juma的黑猩猩开始将草插入耳朵和直肠，这种无实际生物学功能的行为迅速在群体中传播。研究人员认为，这种模仿行为可能有助于加强社交联系，类似于人类的社交文化。类似的现象曾在2010年由一只叫Julie的黑猩猩引发，显示出这种行为可能通过社会学习传递。研究表明，这种无功能性的文化趋势可能源自黑猩猩学习新技能的能力，尤其是在圈养环境下。非功能性的动物文化趋势并非黑猩猩独有，其他动物如虎鲸和海豚也有类似行为。研究动物文化有助于理解人类自身的社会行为。

44521108.article_content:
'Chimpfluencers' Are Sticking Grass in Their Ears And Butts in Latest Viral Trend
Nature
10 July 2025
By
Michael Irving
Chimps have been seen following a bizarre new trend.
(Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
If chimpanzees had access to TikTok, the platform might soon be flooded with videos of 'chimpfluencers' wearing grass in their ears and butts – the latest trend going around a chimp sanctuary in Africa.
In August 2023, at the Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust sanctuary in Zambia, a trendsetting chimp named Juma was seen sticking a piece of grass into his ear, deep enough to stay there on its own. Within a week the fad went viral, as four other chimps in the group started copying his unusual accessory.
Not to be outdone, later that month Juma debuted a risqué variation: he inserted a blade of grass into his rectum, and left it dangling. This unorthodox trend also caught on, with five other chimps adopting the strange new fashion.
Related:
Bored Capuchin Monkeys Are Kidnapping Howler Babies in Weird New 'Trend'
The behavior fascinated researchers observing the captive chimpanzees (
Pan troglodytes
) . The grass didn't seem to serve a biological purpose – they weren't scratching itchy ears or butts, for example. Instead, the team hypothesizes that it might serve a social purpose.
"By copying someone else's behavior, you show that you notice and maybe even like that individual. So, it might help strengthen social bonds and create a sense of belonging within the group, just like it does in humans,"
says
Edwin van Leeuwen, biologist at Utrecht University in the Netherlands.
A chimp showing off its trendy new ear grass. (Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
Intriguingly, the event wasn't the first time Chimfunshi chimps had decorated their orifices with grass. An original trendsetter named Julie started the whole grass-in-ear thing way back in 2010, which caught on with seven other chimps. The behavior continues to this day among the group, even after Julie's death.
This seems to be a case of
social learning
and
cultural transmission
– after all, only one of the four groups observed back then exhibited the behavior, even though all lived in similar conditions. Weirdest of all is that more than a decade after Julie, Juma seems to have come up with the idea independently, since his group never had contact with hers.
The researchers suggest that fads with no clear purpose could be a holdover from the important ability to learn new
survival skills
. It's telling that wild chimps haven't been observed following 'useless' trends – only captive ones seem to have enough time on their hands.
"Chimpanzees can socially learn novel skills and primarily use them in contexts of personal interest, like nut-cracking and termite fishing," the researchers
write in a paper
about their observations.
"Yet, when selection pressures relax (e.g., due to systematic provisioning in captive care), chimpanzees may extend their social learning occasionally to behaviors without direct instrumental utility."
Non-functional
cultural trends
aren't unique to chimps either. In recent years, orcas have been seen
wearing dead salmon
on their heads like hats, and
sinking boats
in European waters – both of which seem to be fads.
A group of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (
Tursiops aduncus
) in South Australia started '
tail-walking
' along the surface of the water after one of them observed captive dolphins that had been trained to do the trick. Wild dolphins continued to perform the feat for decades afterwards, indicating the trend had been passed down culturally.
Studying animal cultures could help teach us more about our own. After all, is sticking grass in your butt really that different from
planking
or
eating laundry detergent pods
?
The research was published in the journal
Behaviour
.

data.title: Why LLMs Can't Write Q/Kdb+: Writing Code Right-to-Left
data.author: gabiteodoru
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）在编写q/kdb+代码时遇到的挑战，主要问题是这些语言采用从右到左且无运算符优先级（RL-NOP）的计算顺序。这种顺序与Python等语言不同，导致LLMs常常生成错误的代码。例如，LLMs在处理表达式时可能生成类似`0.5*y+x/(2*y)`的Python代码，而在q/kdb+中应为`(0.5*y)+x%2*y`。文章指出，RL-NOP是APL及其衍生语言的设计选择，但LLMs难以适应这种编码方式。

作者认为，LLMs在处理RL-NOP语言时的问题不仅限于翻译，还涉及生成代码的顺序。尽管可以通过“UI层”来处理这种转换，但经济激励不足、训练数据稀缺以及模型架构限制使得短期内难以解决这一问题。

为解决此问题，文章提出了一种名为Qython的 pragmatic桥接方案，类似于处理阿拉伯语和希伯来语的方法。这种方案可能为LLMs在处理RL-NOP语言时提供一种实际的解决途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在处理非线性思维、代码生成以及面对不同编程范式时的能力和局限性。

不同观点：
• clord认为，人类编写代码时常常采用非线性的方式，例如从数据或返回值开始逆推，而LLMs目前无法做到这一点，可能会通过从头重写来掩盖其不足。他推测未来的LLMs可能会在非线性结构中工作，或找到将非线性输出映射回线性顺序的方法。

• FeepingCreature指出，Claude模型在编写Python代码时会插入不必要的import语句，因为它在试探性地导入可能稍后需要的模块。

• trjordan提出，训练数据集的大小可能也是影响因素，并建议对q/kdb+等语言与类似大小的左至右语言的错误进行量化分析。

• briandw认为，基于扩散的模型（如diffusion-coder）有能力处理右至左的编码，但目前尚未实现。

• impossiblefork建议通过共享IP或随机IPv6地址来解决监控问题，以使IP不再是个人可识别信息。

• aghilmort讨论了主流模型在可逆因果推理方面的不足，并提出了一些技巧和方法来改善模型的表现，例如利用已知的语言技巧、因果标记和超token等。

• nxobject提到在Lisp语言中遇到的不匹配括号问题。

• am17an指出代码生成中随机插入空格的问题，并认为这是由于不同长度的空格标记所致。

• knome提到其通过向LLMs输入自制的forth-like语言来测试模型解析和生成代码的能力，观察到模型从非常差到逐渐改善的过程。

补充讨论：
• LLMs在处理非线性思维和右至左编程范式时的局限性和潜在改进方法。
• 不同模型在面对语法复杂性和不熟悉范式时的认知负荷问题。
